# Testing Tracker

Two validation levels are required for every interface. See `AGENT.md` for the full rule.

- **Tested=Yes** — Go unit/integration tests exist and pass (`go test`).
- **Validated=Yes** — a live connection or end-to-end test confirmed the interface works with a real or simulated backend.

Do not mark **Validated=Yes** based solely on unit tests.

---

## Pi-prompt descendant-only stall bound (autonomous.descendant_stall_seconds)

New config key and stop detector (pi-prompt family only): a worker attempt whose runner has ended, whose working descendants are still alive, and has no other evidence of life is reaped as an infrastructure failure after `descendant_stall_seconds` (default 2700) and retried via the `auto_fix_retries` budget. Config surface: YAML, REST `GET`/`PUT` config, MCP `autonomous_config_set`, CLI `config set`, comm `configure`, PWA settings card (5 locales).

## Voice transcription errors and chunking

`POST /api/voice/transcribe` changed its error contract. A failed transcription is HTTP 502 with a JSON body `{error, cause, hint, detail, latency_ms}`, where `cause` is `timeout`, `killed`, `out_of_memory`, `ffmpeg_missing`, `backend_error` or `unknown`. The deadline now scales with the audio (5 minutes, or twice the audio length, capped at 30 minutes). Local whisper splits audio longer than the new `whisper.chunk_seconds` (default 120, 0 disables). The PWA keeps a failed recording with Retry and Discard. A failed or slow request writes one `[voice] transcribe failed:` or `transcribe slow:` log line. The how-to is `docs/howto/voice-input.md` and the flow is `docs/flow/voice-transcribe-flow.md`.

Test conditions for every row below: no model download, no real ffmpeg and no network. Go tests use a stub `Transcriber` or a fake `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` script in a temp directory on `PATH`; the PWA tests run under `node --test` with a stubbed `fetch`. Run on 2026-10-27 from the repository root with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR`. Tested is Yes where the named tests pass. Validated is No on every row: no live daemon with a real whisper model was run against a long recording, so none of this was seen working end to end.

## Autonomous triage — records, pass, alert, and the read on every surface

The engine keeps one triage record per failed or blocked Automaton and serves it on every surface: REST (`GET /api/autonomous/triage`), MCP (`autonomous_triage`), CLI (`datawatch autonomous triage`), comm (`autonomous triage …`) and a triage card in the PWA's Automaton detail view. A triage pass runs on every coordinator tick, filling, refreshing and clearing records; once a record has sat for `autonomous.automation.triage_alert_minutes` (default 30; `0` = off), one triage alert per episode goes through the existing alert sink. The record is a read: nothing on this list starts, retries or edits anything. The operator reference is `docs/operations.md` (section *Triage records*), the API contract `docs/api/autonomous.md` (section *Triage records*), the mobile contract `docs/api/mobile-surface.md` (section *Triage records (Automata surface)*) and the how-to pointer `docs/howto/automation-tab.md`.

Every Tested row below was run on 2026-10-27 with Go 1.27.2 (linux/amd64) or Node 24.15.0, from the repository root, with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR` in front of each command. All tests use fakes only: a spy store, fake Automata, fake HTTP servers, and the alert clock advanced with fake time. No test starts a live daemon or a real worker, so **no row is Validated**.

Run everything at once:

```sh
env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/mcp/ ./internal/router/ ./cmd/datawatch/ -run 'Triage' -count=1
env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR node --test internal/server/web/app-triage.test.js
```

**Mobile-Parity: filed.** `dmz006/datawatch-app` issue [#284](https://github.com/dmz006/datawatch-app/issues/284) — filed 2026-10-27 per the daemon repo's standing Mobile-Parity Rule (AGENT.md; no relevant pre-existing issue to comment on). The body filed, in abridged form:

> `feat(automaton-detail): triage card for failed/blocked records`
>
> Server added `GET /api/autonomous/triage` (filters `automation_id`, `prd_id`, `status=failed|blocked`; body `records` newest first + `alert_minutes`), the MCP tool `autonomous_triage`, the CLI `datawatch autonomous triage`, the comm verb `autonomous triage`, a PWA triage card (`triageCardHtml`), and the config key `autonomous.automation.triage_alert_minutes` (default 30, 0 = off). Acceptance: the Automaton detail view shows the card — status, failed task, first-seen, alert time, the four retry budgets, the notes — in en and at least one more locale; a record that disappears clears the card.

### Monitoring and observability

What exists today for the triage feature:

- **The triage record read.** `GET /api/autonomous/triage` (REST) and `autonomous_triage` (MCP) return every stored record plus the effective `alert_minutes`, newest first, with the same filters on both. The CLI and the chat verb read the same route. An operator or an agent can poll it to see what is stuck, why, and whether the alert has already fired (`alerted_at`).
- **The alert on the poll pass.** Once a failed or blocked Automaton has sat for `autonomous.automation.triage_alert_minutes` (default 30, 0 = off), the coordinator's triage pass raises one `warn` alert for that episode and stamps `alerted_at` on the record. It reaches the same alert sinks as the other coordinator alerts.
- **Audit entries.** The triage pass writes no operator audit entry of its own: it fills, refreshes and clears records in the store and raises the alert. Each read of the route does appear in the HTTP access log (`GET /api/audit/access`, MCP `audit_access_query`) like any other request, with its principal. A record that fails to save or clear is written to the daemon log.

Why no new stats field, Monitor card or Prometheus counter yet: the record read and the alert already answer "what is stuck" and "was I told", and the only candidate numbers (records by status, alerts raised) are derived from that same read. A counter or card added now would be a second source that can disagree with the record. Nothing has run against a live daemon over a wall-clock episode (see the pending live checks below), so there is no observed load or failure pattern to size a metric around. When a live run shows one (for example alerts being missed, or the pass running slowly), the first addition would be a count of records by status in the stats payload, with the Monitor card and the Prometheus counter following from it.

## Shared navigation mobile fit

The bottom navigation bar of the PWA now fits 320 to 414 px phones: six equal buttons, labels that truncate with an ellipsis, and a 40 px minimum tap width. The how-to is `docs/howto/navigation-mobile-fit.md`, the plan is `docs/plans/2026-10-25-shared-nav-mobile-fit.md`, and the run records are in `docs/testing/runs/shared-nav-mobile-fit/`. The detailed check steps are in `docs/testing.md` under "Shared navigation mobile fit — phone widths".

Test conditions for every row below, unless a row says otherwise:

- **Daemon:** `Version` 9.11.0 in `cmd/datawatch/main.go` (line 119). The binary was built from the branch with `go build -o bin/datawatch ./cmd/datawatch/`. The code under test is the post-fix tree, `a7cc30e4`, and nothing under `internal/` has changed since (`git diff --stat a7cc30e4 HEAD -- internal/` is empty).
- **Sandbox:** an isolated local daemon started by `scripts/e2e-pwa.sh` on loopback, from `testdata/datawatch.yaml`. No production daemon was used. Runs used `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR`.
- **Browser:** headless Chrome at `/usr/bin/google-chrome`, 100 percent zoom only.
- **Viewports:** gate 320x568, 360x740 and 390x844 in light and dark; baseline 768x1024, 1024x768 and 1280x800 in light and dark; report-only 320x568, 360x740, 375x667, 390x844, 414x896 and 768x1024 in dark.
- **Named checker:** `scripts/test-stories/pwa/shared-nav-mobile-fit.mjs` now exists (commit `cccbd9f0`) but is a wrapper around the probe `shared-nav-mobile-fit-probe.mjs`. Its findings are the probe's, not the spec's.

Tested is Yes only where the node unit test `internal/server/web/app-shared-nav.test.js` covers the row: it checks the `title` attribute on each nav button and the `.nav-label` ellipsis rule in `style.css`, by reading `index.html` and `style.css` (2 of 2 passed under `node --test` on 2026-10-25). Nothing in the Makefile, the scripts or CI runs that test, so it is run by hand. No Go test covers the bar. The gate is an end-to-end browser test, so it is recorded as Validated, not Tested. Tested and Validated are set only from runs that happened on 2026-10-25.

## Lane fill — shadow mode first (automatic lane filling)

Lane fill runs the planner on every coordinator poll and records what it would start on each idle lane. In `shadow` mode (the default) it starts nothing; in `on` mode it starts work through the existing admission path; in `off` it does nothing. The rules are in `docs/plans/2026-10-24-lane-fill-shadow-mode.md` and the operator procedure is in `docs/howto/automation-lane-fill.md`.

Every Tested row below was run on 2026-10-24 with Go 1.27.2 (linux/amd64) and Node.js on the same machine, from the repository root, with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR` in front of each command. The Go tests use fakes only: a fake starter that records calls, a fake pool evidence source, a fake session lister and host lister, a fixed clock, and temporary directories for the decision records. No test starts a live daemon, a real model host or a real worker. The PWA rows are Node tests of the rendering and escaping functions in `internal/server/web/app.js`, not a browser session.

The Shadow mode test `TestLaneFillShadowLoopPollsOnItsOwn` was intermittent before the final gate; its row gives the cause and the fix. After the fix every Go and node group passes in the final gate run.

**No row is Validated.** Every live check is still pending: the one-day shadow comparison against the supervisor's own lane fill (the criteria are in the how-to) has not been run, no sandbox daemon has been run in each mode, and nobody has looked at the Lane fill card in a running PWA. The Notes column says so for each row. The smoke row is not Tested either: its test has not been written.

## Start evidence and busy probe — next patch above main

A claude-code worker in a long silent first tool call now counts as started. The start-confirm tracker takes a tool line, a running or result line, a spinner, a new child process of the runner, a pane change or a channel event after delivery as evidence of work, and measures the silence from the last such evidence. An adopted session is measured from its last evidence of life, not from adoption. The busy probe keeps a delivered claude-code one-shot worker in Running while its pane shows work.

Both validation levels are listed. Every row is Tested by unit tests run on 2026-10-24 with Go 1.27.2 (linux/amd64), using `go test ./cmd/datawatch/ ./internal/session/ -count=1 -v -run '^(…)$'` with the exact names listed below. The start scenarios run on a fake clock with fixed panes and a fixed process tree. The busy probe tests use `NewFakeTmux` and a fake child-process check. Nothing starts a real tmux server, no daemon was restarted and no live worker was run. **Validated is No on every row: a live check of a claude-code worker in a long silent tool call on a sandboxed daemon, and of an adopted worker across a daemon restart, is still needed.**

## Orphan sweep session id comparison — next patch above main

The orphan sweep, the reset that ends a task's live sessions, boot adoption and the task lookup by session id now compare session ids by their short form (the text after the last hyphen) on both sides. Before this, the lister's full id and the short id a task stores never matched, so a live Claude worker bound to a task was ended after the orphan grace period. The sweep also logs once per process when the two id forms differ.

Both validation levels are listed. Every row is Tested by unit tests run on 2026-10-24 with Go 1.27.2 (linux/amd64), using `go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -v -run '^(…)$'` with the exact names listed below. The tests use fakes and fixed clocks only: a fake session table (`liveFake`) standing in for the lister and killer, temp directories and a fake audit sink; no live daemon and no production store was used. The Go test run was made with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR` set. **Validated is No on every row: a live check of a real worker running past the orphan grace period, with the daemon's own lister and killer, is still needed.**

## Automata progress dashboard — unreleased

The progress dashboard reads the Automata list, the backlog table and the explicit waits file and returns one metrics object (counts by kind, rates per active day, utilization, lead time, inactive windows, known versus estimated work left, a completion range) plus a saved daily trend. Operator guide: `docs/howto/automata-progress.md`. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (Phase 8).

Both validation levels are listed. Every row is Tested by unit tests run on 2026-10-23 (Go 1.27.2, Node 24.15.0, Python 3.14.4, linux/amd64) with fakes and fixtures only: in-process fake Automata sources, `httptest` servers, a fake clock and a fixed fixture under `internal/autonomous/testdata/progress/`; no test reads the live Automata store or the live plans registry. **Validated is No on every row: a live sandbox run of the end-to-end story (real finished Automata, a real backlog file and waits file, a daemon left running across a day boundary, the card open in a browser) has not been done by anyone yet and is still owed.**

## Judge routing policy and time limit (Unreleased)

The judges (the Automaton guardrail, plan review and other autonomous judges) have their own role in the verifier routing policy, a backend list of their own (`autonomous.judge_policy`), a 30-minute time limit per run (`autonomous.judge_timeout_seconds`), one attempt per backend, warning alerts on each timeout and an error alert plus a `needs_review` hold when every backend has timed out. The how-to is `docs/howto/judge-policy.md`.

Every row below is **Validated: No**. No live run against a sandbox daemon has been made. The lifecycle rows run the whole judge flow on fakes: a real in-memory capacity ledger with one slot per backend, a fake judge session, a fake clock and a recording alert sink. The surface rows check that every operator surface carries the two settings with the same defaults and wording.

Test conditions for every row below: `go test -count=1` on the branch, with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR`; the JavaScript rows with `node --test`. All rows passed on 2026-10-26.

## Task failure escalation policy: engine, interfaces and operator review (Unreleased)

A task that keeps failing moves up a ladder of workers, is held for operator review at a set failure count, and is then resolved by a retry (optionally with a changed spec, worker or file scope) or a cancel. The policy is set at three levels: task, Automaton and daemon default.

Every row below is **Validated: No**. None of these interfaces has had a live run against a sandbox daemon yet. The opt-in live smoke test is added by a separate task, and each Notes cell says what the live check must confirm.

Live check: a real failing worker is held at the configured count, and retry and cancel act on it. |

Roles tag an LLM registry entry with the workloads it serves; priority orders a session in the capacity wait queue.

## Capacity rate ceilings and the admission Decision query

Rate-ceiling pools, the `Decision` result and the non-blocking admission query (`Ledger.Check`, `GET /api/capacity/admission`) are in the next patch above main. Operator guide: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md`. Every row is Tested by unit tests only, using an in-process ledger and `httptest` servers with fake clocks or short windows. Validated is No: no run against a live daemon with a real metered backend has been done, so a real ceiling being hit and the window freeing is owed.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |

## Automata tags: nested tag registry, per-Automaton assignment, browse and bulk tag

Tags are managed objects (`id`, `name`, `parent_id`, `color`, `description`) persisted to `tags.jsonl`; an
Automaton carries several (`tag_ids`). Deleting a tag with child tags is refused, deleting a tag still assigned
to Automata is refused with a count, and a move that would make a tag its own ancestor is refused. Operator
guide: `docs/howto/automata-tags.md`.

Both validation levels are listed. Each unit row is Tested; none is Validated: a live run against a sandbox
daemon, through each surface, is still owed, and the live rows below say exactly what that run must show.

## Quality gate: shell-run command, invalid baselines, name-based regression, gate_disagreement

The gate's test command runs through a shell in the project directory, a baseline that cannot produce
usable results is recorded as an invalid gate (it only warns and never blocks), regressions are compared by
failing test name and confirmed by one re-run, and `autonomous.gate_disagreement` (`warn` or `block`)
decides what a verifier-passed task does when the gate confirms a regression. Operator guide:
`docs/operations.md` → "Quality gate".

Each row is unit-tested and none is Validated: a live daemon run with a real gate command, through each
surface, is still owed.

A missing directory and a timeout are unusable runs. Go and node output are parsed into counts and failing test names. `TestRunTests_RealGoModule` builds and runs a real Go module with one passing and one failing test. | Unit + real subprocess | **Yes** (`internal/pipeline/quality_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |
| Baseline validity: valid versus invalid | `TestClassifyBaseline_ExitNonZeroNoTests`, `TestClassifyBaseline_ZeroTestsFound`, `TestClassifyBaseline_PackageSetupFailureOnlyIsInvalid` | `go test ./internal/pipeline/ -count=1 -run 'TestClassifyBaseline'` | A non-zero exit that names no failing test, a run with no tests found and a package-level setup failure are invalid. A run that finished with named failing tests is valid. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/pipeline/quality_test.go`) | | **No** — live daemon run pending | |

## Observer mobile fit

The Observer view — System Statistics in particular — never fitted a phone. The
full-profile matrix run on 2026-10-22 (284 scenario runs against an unfixed tree)
reproduces the operator report: the `system-stats-phone` scenario (System Statistics
on a 360×640 phone) fails with a page-level horizontal scroll plus sub-40px tap
targets, clipped text and overlaps — 29,968 findings total, in 68 groups across all
five check dimensions (page-scroll 1, clipped-text 16, tap-target 45, overlap 4,
interaction 2). These rows are the failing baseline; the fix task appends new rows
when it lands. Per-group causes: `docs/plans/2026-10-22-observer-mobile-fit.md`.

## Phase 4 - model-tier defaults

An Automation carries default model settings for the member Automata it runs. The
Automation tier sits between the Automaton and the global default for the execution
backend, model and effort and for the verification LLM, `verifier_source` gains
`automation`, task run records gain `executor_source`, and an optional planning pair
is used only when a member is decomposed. Two set operations, `set_llm` and
`set_verification_llm`, exist on the REST, MCP, CLI and comm surfaces. Design:
`docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (Phase 4).

Each test row is built and unit-tested, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live
row is opt-in and is the run still owed.

pipeline. File on `dmz006/datawatch-app` when the model-tier branch merges:

> `feat(automation): model-tier defaults and executor_source`
>
> Server added two operations on an Automation:
> `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_llm` (body `backend?`, `model?`, `effort?`,
> `planning_backend?`, `planning_model?`) and
> `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_verification_llm` (body `backend?`, `model?`,
> `effort?`). Both also take `expected_version?`, `actor?` and `reason?`. Fields
> are presence-aware: an omitted field is kept and an empty string clears it.
> `expected_version` is optional (omitted or `0` skips the check, a stale
> positive value is `409`). Allowed while the Automation is `draft`, `active`,
> `paused` or `blocked` (otherwise `409`); `400` for no setting field, a planning
> field on `set_verification_llm`, an unknown backend or a bad effort.
> New Automation fields on `/api/automations`: `backend`, `model`, `effort`
> (execution), `planning_backend`, `planning_model` (used only when decomposing
> a member), `verification_backend`, `verification_model`, `verification_effort`.
> Resolution order for the execution backend, model and effort and for the
> verification LLM: task, story, Automaton, Automation, global.
> The verifier source on a task's `verification` object gains the value
> `automation` (`task | story | prd | automation | global | pool`). Task run
> records gain `executor_source` (`task | story | prd | automation | global`),
> also present in the session status Automaton block.
> Acceptance: Android and iOS show `executor_source` beside the verifier source
> on a task and on the session status view, treat an unknown value as plain text,
> and, when they gain an Automation view, offer both set operations with an
> explicit clear action and surface the `409` and `400` messages. The PWA shows
> `executor_source` as an Executor line today and has no Automation view, so
> setting the defaults stays API-only until the PWA Automation view exists.
>
> Localization Rule: new key `status_executor_label`, English "Executor". The
> de, es, fr and ja bundles carry the English placeholder; please supply real
> translations in the app's own bundles.

## Automation view

The Automation view is the first sub-tab of the Automata tab in the PWA (the bottom
navigation has no Automation button), left of the Automata and Templates sub-tabs. It lists
Automations, draws each one as a pipeline strip, drives the control operations and has
a create and edit form. It is built in `internal/server/web` and covered by node tests;
there is no browser test in these rows. Design:
`docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (PWA).

Each test row below was run and passes, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live
row is the run still owed.

**Mobile-Parity: owed, not yet filed.** Issues are not filed from this
pipeline. File on `dmz006/datawatch-app` when the Automation sub-tab branch merges:

> `feat(automation): Automation sub-tab (list, pipeline strip, controls, create and edit)`
>
> The PWA gained an Automation view, the first sub-tab of the Automata tab (there is no Automation button in the main navigation). It uses these REST endpoints:
> `GET` and `POST /api/automations`; `GET`, `PUT` and `DELETE /api/automations/{id}`;
> and `POST /api/automations/{id}/{activate|pause|resume|cancel|skip_member|insert_member|remove_member|reorder_edges|approve_insert|set_llm|set_verification_llm}`.
> Member kinds are `prd` (an Automaton), `automation` (a nested Automation), `fork`
> and `join`. A join carries `on_branch_failure`, one of `all_must_succeed`
> (default), `any_one_is_enough` or `continue_anyway`.
> Cancel requires an explicit `cancel_in_flight` (`true` ends the member sessions
> that are running, `false` leaves them running). There is no default: the app
> must always ask. A `409` on any write means the Automation changed since it was
> loaded; show the server's message and offer a reload, do not retry. A `400`
> shows the server's message on the form.
> Strip rules: members draw as a chain joined by `on_complete` connectors; a fork
> draws its branches in parallel lanes and a join closes them and shows its rule;
> a nested Automation is an expandable level; members in the active positions are
> highlighted; an edge that was not taken is dashed.
> New locale keys: every key with the prefix `automation_`, plus `nav_automation`.
> The de, es, fr and ja bundles in the datawatch repository
> (`internal/server/web/locales/`) already carry translations the app can mirror.
> Acceptance: Android and iOS show the Automation list with status, progress,
> blocked reason and budget; show the pipeline strip with chain, fork lanes, join
> and expandable nested levels; offer pause, resume, cancel (with the explicit
> choice), skip, insert, remove, reorder and approve; offer create and edit with
> linear, fork, join and nested members, default models and a budget policy;
> handle `409` with a reload prompt; and treat an unknown status or member kind as
> plain text.

## Phase 3b — control operations

Operator control of a running Automation: `pause`, `resume`, `cancel` (with a required
in-flight choice), `skip_member`, `insert_member` (with `agent_insert_policy` and the
one-urgent-at-a-time lane), `remove_member`, `reorder_edges` and `approve_insert`, on the
REST, MCP, CLI and comm surfaces, plus the `autonomous.automation.agent_insert_policy`
setting. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (the Phase 3b
sections).

Each test row is built and unit-tested, and none is Validated. Validated is filled in by
the operator's live run, with its date, per the rule at the top of this file. The live
row is opt-in and is the run still owed.

Resume routes members that ended meanwhile and starts the next. Skip follows `on_complete` (default), `on_blocked` or `on_failed`. Remove and reorder refuse members that have started. A stale `expected_version` is a 409. pipeline. File on `dmz006/datawatch-app` when the 3a branch merges:

> `feat(automation): fork/join branches + nested Automations`
>
> Member objects on `/api/automations` gain `kind` (`prd`, `automation`, `fork`,
> `join`; omitted = `prd`), `automation_id`, `fork_members`, `join_members` and
> `on_branch_failure` (`all_must_succeed` default, `any_one_is_enough`,
> `continue_anyway`). `GET /api/autonomous/status` `automations[]` rows gain
> `active_cursors` (`member_id`, `prd_id` or `automation_id`, `status`) and
> `join_wait` (`join_member_id`, `rule`, `pending_branches`, `failed_branches`,
> present only while a join waits). `current_member_id` / `current_prd_id` /
> `current_prd_title` remain, derived from the first active cursor. Stale-version
> updates return `409`.
> Acceptance: Android and iOS render parallel branches and nested levels in the
> pipeline strip, read `active_cursors` and `join_wait`, and do not assume
> `current_member_id` alone. The PWA has no Automation view in this phase, so
> the pipeline strip is API-only until Phase 6.

## Restart keeps claude-code workers — unreleased

A daemon restart no longer ends in-flight claude-code Automaton workers: echo
suppression uses the persisted task delivery time and task text, and live
delivered-task sessions are adopted on resume.

## Restart during launch: boot gate and start-confirm bound — unreleased

A worker whose first launch was held, so its pane holds only a bare shell, is no longer adopted at boot. A live session is adopted only once its agent has started, and an adopted claude-code session is held to the start-confirm bound. A launch still in flight at shutdown is drained within a fixed 15 s grace. Operator guide: `docs/operations.md` (Restart safety). The live check is the restart matrix row in the section below.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Agent-started predicate | `TestAgentStarted*` (11 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/session/ -count=1 -run '^TestAgentStarted'`; fake tmux and output fixtures | A session counts as started when its agent process runs in the pane, or it has a channel-ready event, a delivered task or a first assistant turn. A bare shell with no output reads as not started, and an unknown session reads as not started. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/session/agent_started_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | No real pane was used. |
| Boot adoption gate | `TestBootAdoptionGate*` (4 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestBootAdoptionGate'`; fake session list and killer | A live session is adopted only when its agent has started. A live bare shell is ended through the killer and its task is reset to pending with the start-failure reason, with the retry count and start failures unchanged. A session with its agent running but no first turn is adopted, not killed. With no agent-started hook wired, a live session is adopted as before. | Unit | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/boot_adoption_gate_test.go`) | Pass | **Partly** - see the live row | |
| Adopted session is waited on under the start-confirm bound | `TestAdoptedSession*` (2 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestAdoptedSession'`; fake clock and panes | A healthy adopted session runs to completion under the bound. | Adopted start failure counts against the start budget | `TestAdoptedStartFailure*` (5 tests) | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/autonomous/ -count=1 -run '^TestAdoptedStartFailure'`; fake clock and panes | A session that stays in `waiting_input` with no assistant turn past the limit is ended and counted as a start failure against the start retry budget. The silent window is measured from the task's launch time. ## Daemon restart matrix: in-flight work across a restart

A sandbox harness, `scripts/restart-matrix.sh`, restarts a throwaway daemon with one unit of autonomous work in each of twelve states and records what became of it. Operator guide: `docs/operations.md` (Restart safety). Findings and the open choices: `docs/plans/restart-matrix-findings.md`. The unit rows cover the two defects the matrix found; the live rows are the matrix itself. Every live run used a fake backend for planner, worker, verifier and guardrail judge, on one machine, with one run per cell, so Validated is Partly, not Yes: no real model, no real terminal UI session, no systemd unit and no real service-manager kill was involved.

| Feature | Test Name | Test Conditions | Description | Test Type | Tested? | Pass/Fail? | Validated? | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## WS output-scope unsubscribe contract — test-only flake fixed (BL550)

The unsubscribe contract: when a client sends `unsubscribe` for a session, its subscription for that session is removed, this client's screen-capture pipeline for that session is cancelled, and further output frames are stopped for that session only — the client keeps receiving frames for sessions it is still subscribed to, the other session's capture is not cancelled, and other clients on the hub are unaffected. Short and full session IDs refer to the same session both when unsubscribing and when matching delivery (`a1b2` ≡ `testhost-a1b2`), and unsubscribing an id the client never subscribed is a no-op. The Release-CI flake in `TestWSOutputScope_UnsubscribeStopsDeliveryAndCancelsCapture` (subtest `same_id`, failed in 0.01 s, passed locally) was a scheduling race in the test harness, not in the production path: `findHubClient` snapshotted the hub registry immediately while the hub applies client registration in its own Run goroutine, so the registry write could lag the frames the test had already observed. Fixed in the test file only (`internal/server/ws_output_scope_test.go`): `wsSubscribe` matches the initial `pane_capture` on the exact `session_id` (short/full forms equal) instead of substring-scanning the frame payload; `findHubClient` and the capture-cancel wait poll their real conditions under a deadline bounded by the shared frame timeout with every original assertion preserved at the deadline; and a `t.Cleanup` cancels any still-live capture and waits (bounded poll) until `Hub.ClientCount()` is back to zero so nothing leaks into the next subtest. No production behavior change; no non-test file touched. No live connection was exercised for this fix, so **Validated** stays **No**.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unsubscribe removes the subscription and stops further output frames for that session only — the other subscribed session keeps delivery | **Yes** (`TestWSOutputScope_UnsubscribeStopsDeliveryAndCancelsCapture`, subtests `same_id`, `short unsubscribes full`, `full unsubscribes short`, `internal/server/ws_output_scope_test.go`; no-op for an unknown id in `TestClientUnsubscribe_Direct`) | **No** | `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/server/ -run WSOutputScope -count=50`; `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR go test ./internal/server/ -count=10`; `GOMAXPROCS=2 go test ./internal/server/ -run WSOutputScope -cpu 1,2` | Test-only fix; the production `MsgUnsubscribe` / `client.unsubscribe` path is unchanged |
| Unsubscribe cancels this client's screen capture for that session and no other — a still-subscribed session's capture keeps running | **Yes** (same test: the real cancel is swapped for an observable one, asserts it fires after the unsubscribe acknowledgement and that the other session's cancel entry is still present; `TestClientUnsubscribe_Direct` pins the cancel-count contract on `client.unsubscribe`) | **No** | same as above | Capture goroutine teardown is now explicit in `t.Cleanup` (bounded poll on `Hub.ClientCount() == 0`) so a failed subtest cannot leak its capture goroutine into the next one |
| Short and full session IDs match when unsubscribing (and in delivery) | **Yes** (subtests `short unsubscribes full` and `full unsubscribes short`; id-matching pinned by `TestSessionIDsMatch`) | **No** | same as above | `wsSubscribe` now matches on the exact `session_id` instead of a payload substring that another session's pane text could satisfy |
| Other WS tests sharing the changed helpers audited for the same race | **Yes** and needed no change: `TestWSOutputScope_SubscribedModeFiltersTerminalFrames`, `TestWSOutputScope_ShortAndFullIDsMatch`, `TestWSOutputScope_ConfigDefaultSubscribedForNoHelloClient` (all use `wsSubscribe`); `TestWSOutputScope_MixedClients`, `TestWSOutputScope_AllModeGetsEverySession`, `TestWSOutputScope_HelloBadValueUnchanged`, `TestWSOutputScope_ConfigDefaultReadLive` (same hub/drain helpers) | **No** | same as above (all pass at `-count=50`; package at `-count=10`) | Audit result: no other test asserted on a hub-registry or capture-cancel state without a deadline-bounded wait |

## PRD worktree buildability — `EnsureWorktree` docs-index placeholder

When the daemon creates or reuses a PRD's git worktree, `EnsureWorktree`
(`internal/autonomous/worktree.go`) calls the `prepareWorktree` helper
(`internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare.go`): in repos containing the
`internal/docsindex` package it ensures
`internal/docsindex/assets/docs-bm25-index.json` exists, writing the
same `{}` placeholder `make docs-index` writes, only when the file is
missing (an existing index is never touched), keeps the file
git-ignored (falling back to the worktree's own `info/exclude` if the
ignore rule is absent) and never stages or commits it. Before this,
packages importing `internal/docsindex` failed to build in a fresh
worktree with `pattern assets/docs-bm25-index.json: no matching files
found`, and the daemon reported an otherwise-fine task as failed with
"no new changes to verify".

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Creates when missing — a new or reused worktree gets a `{}` placeholder at `internal/docsindex/assets/docs-bm25-index.json` when the file is absent (same content `make docs-index` seeds) | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_CreatesWhenMissing`, `TestEnsureDocsIndexPlaceholder_CreatesEmptyIndex`, `TestWorktreePrepare_ReuseRecreates` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Covers both fresh creation and recreation on a reused worktree |
| Leaves existing untouched — an existing (custom or fully generated) index is neither rewritten nor mtime-churned when the worktree is reused | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_LeavesExistingUntouched`, `TestEnsureDocsIndexPlaceholder_LeavesExistingFileUntouched` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Never clobbers a real generated index |
| Never staged / stays ignored — placeholder absent from `git status --porcelain` and the index; `git check-ignore -q` passes; exclude line appended to the worktree's `info/exclude` only when the repo `.gitignore` lacks the rule, idempotently (no duplicate on re-prepare) | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_NeverStaged`, `TestPrepareWorktree_GitIgnoredByRepoGitignore`, `TestPrepareWorktree_NonIgnoredRepoGetsExcludeLine`, `TestWorktreePrepare_ExcludeLineNotDuplicated`, `TestAppendGitExcludeLine_IdsAndNoDuplicate` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Prepares never run `git add` or any staging/commit |
| No-op for repos without `internal/docsindex` — no files, no directories, no `info/exclude` mutation in foreign checkouts | **Yes** (`TestWorktreePrepare_NoOpWithoutDocsIndex`, `TestEnsureDocsIndexPlaceholder_IgnoresForeignRepos`, `TestPrepareWorktree_RejectsUnknownRepos` in `internal/autonomous/worktree_prepare_test.go`) | No | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Preparation is non-fatal and must not touch other projects' trees |

## Ancestor CLAUDE.md exclusion for Automaton workers

Claude-code workers belonging to an Automaton are launched with
`--settings '{"claudeMdExcludes":[...]}'` listing every `CLAUDE.md` in a
strict ancestor of the project directory, so another session's guardrail
lines are never read. Interactive sessions get no such flag. See
`docs/operations.md` (Ancestor CLAUDE.md files hidden from Automaton workers).

## Plan review before approval + smoke/final-gate verifier split

Pre-approval plan reviewer: after decompose, a configured LLM reviews the ORIGINAL spec against the plan (requirement coverage, task sizes, dependencies, non-trivial verification scripts, scope outside write_dirs) and records a `plan_review` verdict on the Automaton. Modes `autonomous.plan_review_mode` = `off` (default, no review, approval never affected) / `warn` (verdict recorded and visible, never blocks) / `block` (a `ok:false` verdict refuses approve until it is replaced). A reviewer outage is recorded (`reviewer_failed`) and never blocks in any mode. The plan's own smoke / final-gate verification task is judged by a separate LLM from `autonomous.smoke_verification_backend` / `autonomous.smoke_verification_model`; explicit per-task verifier overrides always win. Surfaces: REST `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/plan-review`, MCP `autonomous_prd_plan_review`, comm `autonomous plan-review <id>`, CLI `datawatch autonomous prd-plan-review <id>` (alias `plan-review`), PWA verdict panel + re-run button + settings fields (en/de/es/fr/ja).

| ok=true × warn/block — verdict persisted on the Automaton, approve proceeds; reviewer cost/tokens recorded on the verdict and on the decision row | **Yes** (`TestPlanReview_Warn_PersistsOkVerdict_NeverBlocks`, asserts `CostUSD` on the appended decision row) | No | `go test` with an in-test reviewer fake | Token/cost fields are 0 when the backend does not report them |

## Tolerant `issues` parser for guardrail verdicts and per-task verification — v9.5.34

The guardrail judge and the per-task verifier used to have to return `issues` as an
array of JSON strings: a single object element — or a bare string/object where an
array was expected — failed the whole verdict/verification decode
(`json: cannot unmarshal object into GuardrailVerdict.issues.0 of type string`),
blocking the PRD even though the work was done. The tolerant decoder
(`internal/autonomous/tolerant_issues.go` — `parseIssues` + custom `UnmarshalJSON`
on `GuardrailVerdict` and `VerificationResult`) accepts all of those shapes and
renders issue objects into readable text, while every other field keeps strict
typing. See CHANGELOG v9.5.34.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Tolerant `issues` decoding — string / object / mixed-array / bare-string / bare-object / bare-number / null shapes normalize to `[]string`; objects render `[severity] file:line: description / message` (deduped, stable order); malformed issues JSON still errors; all other fields (e.g. `"outcome": 5`) still fail strict unmarshal | **Yes** (`TestTolerantIssuesShapes`, `TestTolerantIssuesStrictOtherFields`, `TestIssuesRoundTrip`, `TestIncidentFixtureSizes` in `internal/autonomous/tolerant_issues_test.go`) | **No** (this session did not perform a live rejudge — set to **Yes** with the run date + host once one is actually observed, e.g. a PRD previously blocked by `json: cannot unmarshal object into GuardrailVerdict.issues.0 of type string` rejudged via `POST /api/autonomous/prds/<id>/rejudge`) | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` | Only `issues` is widened; the raw judge text is kept on the verdict in `raw_judge` (16 KiB), and the judge/verifier prompts now instruct "issues must be an array of plain strings, one sentence each, never objects" |

## PWA schedules-flood — `make test-e2e-pwa` (story `scripts/test-stories/pwa/schedule-flood.mjs`, TS-797 spec)

The PWA schedules-flood story: after a WS disconnect/reconnect burst with 20+
seeded sessions, the PWA's `GET /api/schedules` fetches stay coalesced (≤ 5,
independent of session count) and the browser never sees
`net::ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`. Run against **two origins**: (A) the
untrusted self-signed TLS origin, (B) a trusted TLS origin (service worker
controlled). `make test-e2e-pwa` is the local, non-docker route
(`scripts/e2e-pwa.sh`: isolated daemon + `npm ci` + `node schedule-flood.mjs`);
exit code = story's (0 pass / 1 fail / 2 skip).

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Coalesced `/api/schedules` refreshes after WS reconnect — untrusted self-signed TLS origin (A) | No (fix lives in `internal/server/web/app.js` (`_loadSessionSchedules` coalescer); no `node --test` unit test for it) | **Yes** (2026-10-20, `make test-e2e-pwa`, `rc=0`) | Isolated daemon from `bin/datawatch` on fresh 127.0.0.1 ports (config from `testdata/datawatch.yaml`, self-generated TLS); 20 seeded shell sessions (always cleaned up — 20 disposed observed); Playwright + headless Chrome; evidence dir `/tmp/dw-e2e-pwa-04LWs3/evidence/schedule-flood` (removed post-success) | `PASS [A-untrusted-tls] /api/schedules=1 (limit 5) failed-events=0` — one fetch covered the reconnected detail view; zero `ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES`; `/api/sessions` + `/api/stats` 200 after the burst |
| Coalesced `/api/schedules` refreshes after WS reconnect — trusted TLS origin (B, service-worker controlled) | No (same as above) | **Yes** (2026-10-20, same run, scenario B self-generated: openssl throwaway CA + Node TLS proxy + Chrome `--ignore-certificate-errors-spki-list`) | Same harness; `TEST_TRUSTED_TLS` unset → auto-trusted origin; `navigator.serviceWorker.controller` asserted set before request counting | `PASS [B-trusted-tls] sw-controller=true /api/schedules=1 (limit 5)`; 4 `requestfailed` events were non-`ERR_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES` (expected offline-window/WS-reconnect closes), so the bounded-flood assertion held |
| `make test-e2e-pwa` target — local non-docker route, non-zero exit on story failure | No (bash script; no unit test) | **Yes** (2026-10-20, run above) | `make test-e2e-pwa` from repo root; `node v24.15.0`, `npm` present; optional `TEST_TRUSTED_TLS` supported; `TEST_HTTP`/`TEST_TLS`/`TEST_TOKEN` external-daemon mode accepted | `scripts/e2e-pwa.sh` ran `npm ci` then `node schedule-flood.mjs`, propagated rc=0, killed the daemon; on failure it keeps the evidence dir and exits non-zero (story's own code 1 or 2) |

### Baseline measurement — before-fix vs after-fix (connection-drop investigation, 2026-10-20)

The story now also logs peak in-flight concurrency per phase — `load` = page load +
detail-view open; `reconnect` = the WS-disconnect → recover window — so before/after
comparisons diff on one line. Both runs 2026-10-20, 20 seeded sessions, scenario A
(untrusted-TLS origin; the daemon offers HTTP/1.1 only, so the browser's 6-concurrent
per-origin cap applies exactly as on the phone/cellular path). Two binaries with
different embedded `app.js` — no git stash: **before** = `app.js` as of `31d96b1e`
(parent of the fix commit, no `_loadSessionSchedules` coalescer), **after** = HEAD
(`8412e745` coalescer in place), both run via `bash scripts/e2e-pwa.sh schedule-flood`.

| origin | metric | before-fix (no coalescer) | after-fix (HEAD) |
|---|---|---|---|
| A (untrusted TLS) | total `/api/schedules` | **42** (page-load+detail=1, **reconnect-window=41**) | **1** (page-load only; reconnect-window=0) |
| A (untrusted TLS) | peak in-flight, all traffic, reconnect window | 8 | 0 |
| A (untrusted TLS) | peak in-flight `/api/schedules`, reconnect window | 4 | 0 |
| A (untrusted TLS) | story verdict | FAIL (`42 > limit 5`) | PASS, `failed-events=0` |

Evidence: `.scratch/evidence/README.md` (method + pointers), `.scratch/evidence/BASELINE-run-before.log` and `.scratch/evidence/run-after.log` (full run transcripts),
`.scratch/evidence-before/run-1/` (before-run screenshots + daemon log), binaries `.scratch/bin/datawatch-{before,after}`.

**Interpretation (CONFIRMED):** the pre-fix burst is ~41× the post-fix footprint, fired
in the reconnect window, proportional to session count (one un-coalesced fetch per
session update of the active detail view). 41+ requests against a 6-connection
per-origin pool starve the co-residents on that origin — `/api/sessions`, `/api/stats`,
and the WS upgrade handshake itself — which to an operator on cellular looks like the
device "dropped the connection." The flood does **not** by itself sever the WS
transport; it exhausts the shared HTTP pool. Other observed drop-path code — WS stale
watchdog (50 s stale threshold, 20 s ping tick, 50–70 s detection), reconnect backoff,
and the server's 30 s protocol-ping ticker (`internal/server/ws.go` `writePump`) — are
separate, legitimate disconnect/reconnect mechanisms, recorded for the record and not
fixed in this pass. See CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased].

## Observer mobile-fit regression guard — `scripts/test-stories/pwa/TS-817.mjs` (TS-817, wrapper `scripts/test-stories/TS-817.sh`) + desktop guard `scripts/test-stories/pwa/TS-818.mjs` (TS-818)

group, `failed_before_fix: true`), the full Observer `quick` profile matrix
(14 states x 320x568 / 360x740 / 390x844 / 768x1024 dark + 360x740 landscape +
360x740 light + z200 first state), the recorded zoom cells (three-peers
320x568 z130/z200, three-peers 390x844 z200, no-peers 568x320), the named

the three interactions (section-collapse-expand, refresh, rerender-timers).

Observer tracked-selector rects at 1280x800, 1920x1080 and 768x1024 and asserts

## Autonomous completion-guardrail rejudgment — `POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/rejudge` + MCP `autonomous_prd_rejudge`

New endpoint and MCP tool. Re-runs the PRD-completion "rules-review" guardrail for a `blocked` Automaton whose every task in every story is `completed`, without resetting or editing any task. The verdict is durably recorded on the Automaton's decision log (`guardrail_verdict` Decision + save, then a `guardrail_rejudge` Decision attributed to the acting operator) **before** any status change: `pass` clears the blocked reason and completes the Automaton; `block` keeps it `blocked` with the blocked reason set from the new verdict; no verdict (judge error or empty outcome) keeps it `blocked` with its previous reason and returns an error.

## Service worker activate guard — `shouldNavigateOnActivate` in `internal/server/web/sw.js`

On a real cache-name upgrade the new SW must force every controlled window to re-navigate so
installed PWA tabs drop the stale cached app.js. But `activate` also re-runs on a no-op
re-activation (browser re-activates the same SW on restart with no cache change) — the guard keeps
that path from needlessly churning open tabs: `clients.claim()` is still called, but the
`matchAll`/`navigate` loop is skipped when no stale cache key exists. The pure guard is unit-tested
and the `activate` listener is driven end-to-end with a stubbed `self` in `sw.test.js`; the
operator-visible double-load symptom on daemon restart was then verified live in headless Chrome
(CDP, `live-sw-check/` below).

| Test Condition | Unit | Live | Test ID / Location | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Guard: no keys, or only the current key → navigate skipped; current + stale key(s) → navigate; non-array input tolerated | **Yes** | No | `shouldNavigateOnActivate: no keys at all is a no-op re-activation`, `...only the current cache present...`, `...current plus a stale key is a genuine upgrade`, `...multiple stale keys are a genuine upgrade`, `...non-array input is treated as no keys` in `internal/server/web/sw.test.js` | 5 pure-guard tests, `node --test` |
| `activate`: stale cache present → stale caches deleted, `claim()` once, every window navigated exactly once | **Yes** | No | `activate: stale cache present → stale deleted, claim called, every window navigated once` in `internal/server/web/sw.test.js` | Real `activate` listener, stubbed `self`/`caches`/`clients`; also `activate: one window navigate rejecting does not abort the others or the handler` |
| `activate`: no-op re-activation (only current cache, or no caches) → `claim()` still called, **no** navigate | **Yes** | No | `activate: only the current cache present (no-op) → claim called, no navigate`, `activate: no caches at all → claim called, no navigate` in `internal/server/web/sw.test.js` | `matchAll` skipped on the no-op path |
| Live: daemon-restart / reload under an already-activated current-version SW → exactly one document load, no spurious reload | No | **Yes** | `live-sw-check/`: `sw-live.mjs` (Phase B) + `RESULTS.md`; daemon `live-sw-check/config.yaml` (port 18491), log in `daemon-b.log` | Headless Chrome 155.0.8059.39 over CDP (puppeteer-core was absent); CDP `Page.loadEventFired`=1, `navigation entries`=[navigate], `reloadCount` 0, hook log empty. Phase A (fresh install) showed the one-time first-load SW-takeover reload that happens independently of the guard — not a guard-driven navigate |
| Live: genuine cache-name upgrade (new SW, stale cache present) → exactly one SW-driven reload, stale cache purged, new SW controls the page | No | **Yes** | `live-sw-check/RESULTS.md` (Phase C: `sw.js` `CACHE_NAME` bumped to `...-51-livecheck`, daemon rebuilt + restarted) | CDP `frameNavigated` once at +2.1s after the SW update burst (`reloadCount` 1); `caches` ended as [bumped key] only (stale deleted); page-script hook never hit — reload is the guard's `win.navigate`, not app JS. `sw.js` then reverted and rebuilt |

## MCP error-mode parity with REST — BL463 (2026-10-20)

Follow-up to the findings in `docs/plans/2026-10-20-bl463-mcp-drop-findings.md`. Before
this change, many MCP handlers failed "soft": they returned
`mcpsdk.NewToolResultText("Error: ...")` with a nil Go error, so the result carried no
`isError` flag, no tool name, and (for REST-loopback proxies) no upstream HTTP status
or body — the same wire result a successful call would have, and `POST /api/mcp/call`
mirrored that (HTTP 200, `isError:false`) while direct REST returned 4xx/5xx. The
shared helpers in `internal/mcp/errors.go` (`toolError`, `toolErrorf`,
`toolHTTPError`) now return real IsError results named after the tool call,
and the `sx_parity.go` REST-loopback proxy helpers capture and carry the upstream
status + body (truncated at 2048 chars).

| `toolHTTPError` carries the HTTP status + upstream body, degrades to the status text on an empty body, and bounds oversized bodies at 2048 bytes (maxToolErrorBody); the `sx_parity.go` loopback proxy helpers cap their error bodies the same way (boundedErrorBody) | **Yes** | No | `TestToolHTTPError_CarriesStatusAndBody`, `TestToolHTTPError_NoBody`, `TestToolHTTPError_TruncatesOversizedBody`, `TestBoundedErrorBody_TrimsAndCaps` in `internal/mcp/errors_test.go` | PASS |

## Daemon restart safety (live, opt-in) — BL462

Live companion to the BL462 restart audit (`docs/plans/bl462-restart-audit-findings.md`).
It repeats the audit's sequence against a real daemon: start a long claude-code
task session, restart the daemon, and check that the tmux session survives,
the session record is not failed, and the session log keeps growing. The test
is skipped unless `DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1`, so `go test ./...` in CI skips it.

Run it on the daemon's host, against a sandbox daemon (never production), with
the same `TMUX_TMPDIR` as that daemon:

```sh
DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1 DW_BASE=https://127.0.0.1:18443 DW_BASE_TOKEN=... \
  DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD='<command that restarts the sandbox daemon>' \
  go test -count=1 -timeout 20m -run TestBL462_DaemonRestartSurvivesLive -v ./internal/session/
```

Leave `DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD` unset to restart through the operator path
(`systemctl --user restart datawatch`, falling back to `datawatch restart`).
Only do that from an operator shell where that unit is the daemon behind `DW_BASE`.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Daemon restart with a live claude-code task session — tmux session survives, session record not `failed`/`killed`/spurious `complete`, session log grows after restart (re-pipe), task reaches a terminal state if it finishes within the wait | **Yes** (skip path only: `TestBL462_DaemonRestartSurvivesLive` in `internal/session/restart_safety_live_test.go`, run by `.datawatch/verify/bl462-s3-live-restart-test.sh`) | **No** (gated live run not performed; no sandbox daemon was started for it) | `go test` with `DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1` against a live daemon via `DW_BASE`/`DW_BASE_TOKEN`; restart is `systemctl --user restart datawatch` or the `datawatch restart` CLI, or `DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD` for a sandbox | Verifies what the audit verified by hand. Does not cover subprocess sessions (F4) or the capacity lease (F1); the audit's live run of those is in `docs/plans/bl462-restart-audit-findings.md` |

## Boot-resume adopts a live in-progress worker (deterministic + gated live)

Deterministic coverage for the adoption behavior — a daemon restart
resumes a run whose task was `in_progress` with a live worker session:
the live session is **adopted** (task stays `in_progress` on the same
session id, capacity lease re-adopted, **no duplicate spawn**, worker
finishes and the task verifies and completes), a dead session with a
completion marker in its output **goes straight to verification** (no
re-run of finished work), and a dead session without a marker **resets to
`pending`** (the only reset case). All sessions are fakes (map-backed
`alive` function, recording killer, fake output, spawn counter); every
wait is a bounded poll — no fixed sleeps; table-driven across the
`claude-code`, `opencode`, and `pi-prompt` backends; verified green with
`-race -count=3` (three races, no fixed sleeps). The pre-existing
`TestAdoptSessionDecision` (decision table for the same code) is
unchanged.

Gated live companion — one PRD with a long worker, restarted mid-worker
through the operator path (`systemctl --user` / `datawatch restart`) or
`DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD`; asserts the session id is unchanged after
restart, the session is not `killed`, no task is re-issued a new
session, and the task drives to verification/completion.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boot-resume: alive worker adopted — task stays `in_progress`, same session id, `AdoptedSession` set, capacity lease held, idempotent on a second boot | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_AliveAdopted` in `internal/autonomous/adopt_live_session_test.go`; `-race -count=3` | Fake sessions; no production state. Boot scan parked via `SetServerReadyCh` to keep the concurrent paths deterministic (same pattern as `TestRunDedupe`) |
| Boot-resume: dead worker without marker — task reset to `pending`, session id cleared, killer called for the exact session | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_DeadReset` | Table over dead-with-no-output / empty-session / never-started; no marker in the dead output in any case |
| Boot-resume: dead worker that finished during the down window — output carries `DATAWATCH_COMPLETE` → task goes to `verifying`, verifier runs once, **no spawn** | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_FinishedWhileDown` | Completing session is recorded as `complete` in the fake registry; the run finishes `completed` with verifyCount=1, spawnN=0 |
| Boot-resume: adopted task not re-spawned — executor run over an adopted `in_progress` task waits for the existing session (0 spawns), completes after fake completion; two concurrent `Run` calls start exactly one executor and the PRD stays `running` | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestAdoptLive_NoDuplicateSpawn` | `apiFixture` + `countingSpawn`/`recordedKiller`; drainOnCleanup wired. Verified with `-race -count=3` (all green) |
| Restart while a worker PRD task is live — session id unchanged after restart, no second spawn (no task re-issued a session), worker not killed, task drives to verification/completion | **Yes** (skip path only) | **No** (gated live run not performed) | `TestDaemonRestartAdoptsLiveWorkerLive` in `internal/session/restart_adopt_live_test.go`; `DW_LIVE_RESTART_TEST=1` + `DW_BASE` (+ optional `DW_BASE_TOKEN`, `DW_LIVE_RESTART_PROJECT_DIR`, `DW_LIVE_RESTART_CMD`); run with `-timeout 25m`; cleanup kills only its own probe session via the API (no raw tmux kill) | PRD-level counterpart of `TestBL462_DaemonRestartSurvivesLive`: reuses `newBL462LiveClient`, `bl462RestartCommand`, `bl462PollUntil`, `bl462TmuxHasSession` from `restart_safety_live_test.go`. The restart subprocess env is sanitized by `bl462RestartEnv`: TMUX and TMUX_TMPDIR stripped, except the `datawatch restart` CLI fallback which keeps TMUX_TMPDIR (documented exception — the CLI re-execs the daemon in the ambient env and must keep the tmux socket dir) |

## Restart no longer revives stale running Automata — new `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` limit — v9.5.32

At daemon restart, an Automaton left running is now gated: it resumes only if its newest activity is within `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` (default 3600) **and** its project directory still exists; `0` = never auto-resume, `-1` = no age limit (missing dirs still park). Parked Automata become `blocked` with a plain-English reason + operator alert, and each decision (resumed/parked, age, reason) is recorded in the startup log, the decision log, and the autonomous status `boot_resume` list.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Boot resume gate (daemon startup path) — covers running and failed Automata (failed ones whose tasks were all killed by the restart); fresh Automaton resumes; stale (age > limit) parked; `0` parks even fresh; `-1` skips the age test but a missing project directory still parks; park ⇒ `blocked` + `BlockedReason` + operator alert; report records outcome/age/reason | **Yes** (13 tests, including the failed-Automaton path: `TestBootResumeGateFailedFreshRecovered`, `TestBootResumeGateFailedStaleParked`, `TestBootResumeGateCancelledUntouched`, `TestBootResumeGateFailedLimits`; `TestBootResumeGateFreshResumes`, `TestBootResumeGateZeroLimitParksFresh`, `TestBootResumeGateMinusOneSkipsStale`, `TestBootResumeGateStaleParked`, `TestBootResumeGateMissingDirParks`, `TestBootResumeGateDefaultConfig`, `TestBootResumeGateReport`, `TestBootResumeGateAlertOnPark`, `TestDecideBootResumeUnit` in `internal/autonomous/boot_resume_gate_test.go`; plus config-load tests in `internal/config/resume_max_age_test.go`) | **No** | `go test ./internal/autonomous/` and `go test ./internal/config/`; fake store + seeded PRDs aged via timestamps, temp dirs for the missing-directory case | `0` and `-1` are meaningful sentinels (round-trip preserved through config YAML); `DefaultConfig()` returns 3600; a parked Automaton is manually approvable — no silent re-run |
| REST config — `GET /api/config` reports `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds` default 3600; `PUT /api/config` round-trips the key (0 and -1 preserved); `PUT /api/autonomous/config` persists it | **Yes** (3 tests: `TestResumeMaxAge_GetConfigDefaultIs3600`, `TestResumeMaxAge_PutConfigRoundTrip`, `TestResumeMaxAge_PutAutonomousConfigPersists` in `internal/server/resume_max_age_config_surfaces_test.go`) | **No** | `go test ./internal/server/`, real HTTP handler against in-memory config | Written values survive YAML round-trip, so an explicit 0/-1 is not clobbered back to the 3600 default on reload |
| MCP config — `autonomous_config_set` / `autonomous_config_get` accept and return `autonomous.resume_max_age_seconds`, including the 0/-1 sentinels; tool docs mention the key | **Yes** (2 tests: `TestAutonomousConfigSet_ResumeMaxAgeSentinels`, `TestAutonomousConfigTools_DocumentResumeMaxAge` in `internal/mcp/resume_max_age_tools_test.go`) | **No** | `go test ./internal/mcp/`, fake autonomous manager | 0 and -1 pass through unchanged (not clamped to a positive value) |

## Per-tree write lock + same-tree admission + ci-watch own-commit pin — v9.4.0 / v9.5.0

The 2026-10-13 incident (three concurrent PRDs, one working tree) shipped two
cooperating fixes in the 9.4.0/9.5.0 development builds: the per-task tree
writer lock (BL428 Phase 2, `internal/autonomous/tree_lock.go`) and the
PRD-level same-tree admission gate (BL469, `internal/autonomous/tree_admission.go`),
plus the ci-watch own-commit pin (BL423, `internal/autonomous/ci_watch.go`).

## Automata lifecycle outbound webhook sink and peer forwarding — signed HTTPS delivery, allow-list and SSRF guard, bounded retry, federation peer forwarding with loop prevention, config keys and surfaces — Unreleased, shipped disabled (Phase 5 of plans/2026-10-13-prd-lifecycle-events.md)

Both sinks ship disabled (`autonomous.notify.webhook.enabled`, `autonomous.notify.forwarding.enabled` default `false`). Every row below is Tested=Yes from the Go or `node --test` suites named in it, and Validated=No until the live smoke run for that row is performed. Rows the smoke saw say which part under Notes.

**Run provenance (2026-10-25):** evidence is in `docs/testing/runs/lifecycle-webhook-smoke-2026-10-25/`. Both runs used a sandbox daemon built with `go build` from commit `f1d0ceaa` with a clean tree (0 uncommitted paths in both `environment.txt` and `smoke-run.txt`); the later commits change only this tracker and the evidence files, no daemon code. The sandbox has isolated data and home directories and free loopback ports, with a throwaway receiver on 127.0.0.1, on Linux with Go 1.27.2. Run 1, direct: `scripts/release-smoke-lifecycle-webhook.sh` in fresh-sandbox mode (`smoke-run.txt`, `environment.txt`, `forwarding-tests.txt`), all eight steps PASS. Run 2, through the story wrapper in `scripts/test-stories/`: sourced once the way the runner does, against a sandbox daemon started by hand from the same commit, existing-sandbox mode (`story-wrapper-run.txt`), all eight steps PASS and the story result is pass; that mode cannot read the daemon log, so the daemon-log secret scan is in run 1 only. The verification gate run on the final committed tree is saved as `verify-gate-run.txt` in the same directory.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Outbound target guard — allow-list match (exact host or host:port, case-insensitive, no wildcards, empty list allows nothing), URL policy (https only, http only for an allow-listed host, no userinfo, no obfuscated IP spellings), address classes (loopback, link-local, private, Tailscale CGNAT refused unless allow-listed; cloud metadata refused even when allow-listed), dial-time IP re-check against DNS rebinding, redirects never followed, proxy environment ignored, response body capped | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/lifecycle_webhook_guard_test.go`) | No | `go test` with an injected resolver and `httptest` servers; no real DNS | **Observed 2026-10-25 (fresh sandbox):** an allow-listed receiver got the delivery; a host that is not on the list and the cloud metadata address were each refused with 400 at creation; with the list emptied a test-fire was refused and made zero requests at the receiver. **LIVE pending:** a private-address target refused at delivery time and audited as `refused`. Evidence: `smoke-run.txt`. |
| Request signer — `t=<unix>,v1=<hex>` = HMAC-SHA256 over `<t>.<raw body>`, constant-time verification, replay window in both directions, malformed and duplicate fields rejected, errors never echo the header, body or secret | **Yes** (`internal/autonomous/lifecycle_webhook_sign_test.go`) | **Yes** (live-covered part only; the rest is unit-test only, see Notes) | `go test` with a fixed clock | **Validated 2026-10-25 (fresh sandbox, live part only):** the receiver snippet copied from the how-to (executed from the document text itself) accepted the signature of a real delivery, rejected the same request with one byte of the body changed, and rejected a wrong secret; the first delivery's signature also verified against the stored secret and the envelope parsed. **Unit-test only, not observed live:** the replay window in both directions, rejection of malformed and duplicate fields, the constant-time comparison, and the rule that errors never echo the header, body or secret. | MCP `plugin_enable` `managed` arg | **Yes** (`TestPluginEnable_NoManagedSendsNoBody`, `TestPluginEnable_ManagedSendsBody`, `TestPluginEnable_ToolDeclaresManagedArg` in `internal/mcp/plugins_test.go`) | No | Proxy body captured by a test server | Body sent only when the arg is supplied |

**Manual verification steps (live, not yet performed):**
1. Install a service plugin whose manifest lists `managed` in `lifecycle.supported_modes`, with `connection.health_path` and `restart_policy: on-failure`.
2. Set `plugins.enabled: true` and `plugins.managed: [<name>]`; restart the daemon (`systemctl --user restart datawatch`). Expect `GET /api/plugins/<name>` → `service.state` `starting` then `healthy`, and an audit `plugin_service_start`.
3. `kill -9` the child PID. Expect `plugin_service_restart`, a new `pid`, `restarts` incremented, state back to `healthy`.
4. Make the health endpoint return 500 (or block it). Expect `unhealthy`, then `plugin_service_health_fail` after 3 probes and a restart.
5. Make the child exit non-zero on every start. Expect state `failed` and `plugin_service_stop` with `reason: max_restarts` after 6 consecutive failures.
6. `POST /api/plugins/<name>/disable`. Expect `plugin_service_stop` `reason: requested` and the process group gone within `stop_timeout_ms`.
7. Re-enable with `{"managed": true}`, then stop the daemon. Expect the child reaped before the daemon exits.
8. Negative: `POST /api/plugins/<attach-only-plugin>/enable` with `{"managed": true}` → `400`.

**Mobile parity:** No PWA change. The plugin JSON (`service` object) and the enable request body are API contract changes, so the Mobile-Parity Rule applies and a `datawatch-app` issue/comment is required; not filed from this automated run — flagged for the operator (see CHANGELOG v9.0.32).

**Configuration accessibility:** YAML (`plugins.managed`), REST (enable body, runtime) and MCP (`plugin_enable` `managed`) covered. CLI flag, comm-channel command (beyond the generic `rest` passthrough), PWA control and generic config-set support for `plugins.managed` deferred to the operator UI phase.

## Autonomous PRD Split Planning/Execution Backend (v8.20.0)

Added in v8.20.0. Separates the PRD planning backend (`decomposition_profile`, used by Decompose/DecomposeStreaming) from the task-execution backend (`backend`, used by autonomous task session spawning). Resolution order (v8.33.9 priority fix): `prd.DecompositionProfile` (per-PRD, wins) → `manager.cfg.PlanningBackend` (global fallback) → `"ollama"` default. Any registered LLM works for planning — opencode/claude-code spawn a full session with codebase tool access; ollama/openwebui run headless. CLI `prd-set-llm` gained `--decomposition-profile` flag in v8.33.9.

`POST /api/autonomous/prds/{id}/set_llm` — extended with `decomposition_profile` field (validated against inference registry). Available on all surfaces: REST, MCP (`autonomous_prd_set_llm`), CLI (`prd-set-llm --decomposition-profile`), PWA Settings modal, Android/iPhone (via REST).

## PWA Current-Status No-Change Contract (v8.19.8)

`GET /api/sessions/{id}/current-status` — changed in v8.19.8 from HTTP 204 (empty body) to HTTP 200 + JSON `{"no_change":true}` on the two no-op branches (no new output; thin delta). Root cause: RFC 7231 §3.3 forbids a body on 204; Go's `net/http` silently drops it; PWA's `r.json()` threw `Unexpected end of JSON input`. `apiFetch` also hardened to resolve 204/205 → null.

| Test case | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| No new output → HTTP 200 + `no_change:true` — `TestCurrentStatus_NoNewOutput` | **Yes** | No | `internal/server/current_status_test.go` — empty output store; asserts 200 + non-empty body + `no_change:true` | Pins the exact bug: 204 + empty body used to reach PWA as a `r.json()` throw |
| Thin delta (output unchanged since last call) → HTTP 200 + `no_change:true` — `TestCurrentStatus_ThinDelta` | **Yes** | No | Same file — output identical on two consecutive calls; second returns `no_change:true` | Covers the second merged branch of the no-op condition |
| Success path with new output → HTTP 200 + content body | **Yes** | No | `TestCurrentStatus_WithNewOutput_Returns200` in `internal/server/current_status_test.go` — T47 sprint | Live test: start a session, let it produce output, poll endpoint; verify body contains session output and no `no_change` field |

## Multi-provider web search registry (BL391, v8.39.0)

Rewritten in v8.39.0 from the single-provider SearXNG-only design (v8.22.0/BL372).
`internal/websearch` now holds a provider-agnostic `Registry` (SearXNG + Brave
Search API, tried in priority order, extensible), an internal result cache, and
a SQLite usage-tracking store, shared in-process by REST/MCP/stats and by the
standalone `datawatch mcp-search` subprocess (`internal/mcp/search/`, injected
into opencode/goose sessions). The pre-BL391 rows below (`frameScanner`,
`searxngSearch()`, `TestHandleToolsCallNoURL`, etc.) described functions that
no longer exist after the rewrite — this section replaces them.

| Component | Unit tested | Live tested | Unit test coverage | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|

| `BraveProvider.Search()` | **Yes** | No | `TestBraveProviderSearch`, `TestBraveProviderAuthRejected`, `TestBraveProviderRateLimited` in `internal/websearch/brave_test.go` | httptest-backed; test-only `endpoint` field overrides the real API host |
| `Cache` — hit/miss/expiry/per-entry TTL override | **Yes** | No | `cache_test.go`: `TestCacheHitMiss`, `TestCacheKeyDistinguishesProviderQueryLimit`, `TestCacheExpiry`, `TestCacheDisabledViaZeroTTL`, `TestCachePerEntryTTLOverride`, `TestNilCacheIsSafe` | nil `*Cache` always misses (caching-disabled path) |
| `Store` — SQLite usage rollups | **Yes** | No | `store_test.go`: `TestStoreRecordAndSummary`, `TestStoreSummaryCalendarBoundaries`, `TestStoreDailySeriesZeroFilled`, `TestStoreHistoryPaginationAndOrder`, `TestStorePrune`, `TestNilStoreIsSafe` | Calendar boundaries (today/week/month) computed in UTC |
| `Registry.Search()` — priority fallback + cache | **Yes** | No | `registry_test.go`: `TestRegistryPriorityFallback`, `TestRegistrySkipsEmptyResultsNotJustErrors` (direct GH#165 regression guard), `TestRegistryAllProvidersFail`, `TestRegistryCacheHitSkipsLiveCall`, `TestRegistryPriorityOrdering`, `TestRegistryUnknownProviderType`, `TestRegistryNotEnabledWithNoProviders` | A provider that "succeeds" with 0 results is treated as a miss, not a hit |
| `mcp-search` `handle()` — tools/list, tools/call, ping, unknown method/tool | **Yes** | No | `internal/mcp/search/server_test.go`: `TestHandlePing`, `TestHandleToolsList`, `TestHandleToolsCallNoProviders`, `TestHandleToolsCallWithRegistry`, `TestHandleToolsCallUnknownTool`, `TestHandleUnknownMethod`, `TestHandleNotification` | NDJSON transport (one JSON object per line, no Content-Length framing) |
| `mcp-search` `buildRegistry()` — standalone override vs. full config.yaml | **Yes** | No | `TestBuildRegistryStandaloneOverride`, `TestBuildRegistryFromConfigYAML` | Override path (`--url`/env) wins over `config.yaml`'s `providers[]` |
| REST `/api/websearch/providers` CRUD — secret handling | **Yes** | No | `internal/server/websearch_test.go`: `TestWebSearchEnable_DoesNotPersistResolvedSecret`, `TestWebSearchUpdate_ExplicitAPIKeySavedAsGiven`, `TestWebSearchUpdate_OtherFieldDoesNotLeakSecret`, `TestWebSearchProvidersList_ReturnsConfiguredProviders`, `TestWebSearchProvidersList_NeverEchoesResolvedAPIKey`, `TestWebSearchDelete_RemovesProviderWithoutLeakingOthersSecret` | Guards the exact plaintext-secret-leak class of bug: a config save triggered by an unrelated field must never write a resolved `${secret:...}` value back to `config.yaml` |
| opencode/goose injection — `extraMCPSpecs["web_search"]` gated on `webSearchActive` | Partial (config-shape unit only) | **Yes — with an important caveat found live** | `TestBuildRegistryFromConfigYAML` covers the config-load half | **Live finding (2026-10-02, this host):** the per-session `.mcp.json` file the daemon writes into an opencode session's project dir is not actually consumed by opencode — opencode's MCP discovery on this host comes entirely from the global, statically-configured `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc` `mcp` key (native `{type:"local",command:[...],enabled:true}` schema, not a sibling `.mcp.json` file). That global config already has a `searxng` entry running `datawatch mcp-search` with no env override, which DOES correctly load the full multi-provider `config.yaml` registry and is exposed to the model as tool `searxng_web_search` (opencode's own `<server>_<tool>` naming). Not fixed in this release (separate, pre-existing scope); flagged here so it isn't lost. Goose uses a different mechanism (env vars set directly on the goose process, not a config file) and was not independently live-verified this release. |

| PWA Dashboard "Search Usage" card (`_dashRenderWebSearchUsage`) | No | **Pending** | — | Live: Dashboard tab, new `websearch-usage` card in `DASH_CARD_DEFS` |
| PWA Monitor tab "Search Usage" stat card + history modal (`refreshWebSearchStatsCard`, `webSearchOpenHistoryView`) | No | **Pending** | — | Live: Monitor tab, replaces the old flat BL372 web-search tile |

Brave specifically was exercised via the REST test endpoint rather than through opencode, since SearXNG's higher priority (0 < 1) wins the live registry's provider race whenever it succeeds — forcing a live opencode call through Brave specifically would require temporarily disabling the SearXNG provider, not done this pass. |

## v8.31.0 — Automata Memory Integration: Verifier Findings + Child Inheritance

Added in v8.31.0. When `memory_seed.enabled=true` on an Automaton, two new callbacks
fire: (1) after each verification failure, each issue string is written to `prd-shared`
with `role=verifier-finding`; (2) when a child Automaton is spawned via recursive
decomposition, up to 50 entries from the parent's `prd-shared` are seeded into the child's
`prd-shared` before the child decomposes.

| `memoryVerifierFn` NOT called on verify success | Yes | No | `TestBL387_Verifier_NoWrite_OnSuccess` | fn must not fire for OK=true tasks |
| `memoryVerifierFn` NOT called when `memory_seed.enabled=false` | Yes | No | `TestBL387_Verifier_NoWrite_WhenMemorySeedDisabled` | Default disabled state |
| `[verifier-finding]` prefix present in content | Yes | No | `TestBL387_Verifier_ContainsPrefix` | Content always starts `[verifier-finding] <issue>` |
| `memoryVerifierFn` error does not abort retry loop | Yes | No | `TestBL387_Verifier_ErrorDoesNotAbortRetry` | Simulated write failure → executor continues; verifyCount > 0 |
| `memoryScopeSeedFn` called with parent/child PRD IDs + projectDir | Yes | No | `TestBL387_ChildPRD_InheritsParentPRDShared_WhenSeedEnabled` | fromPRDID=parent.ID, toPRDID=child.ID, same projectDir |
| `memoryScopeSeedFn` NOT called when parent `memory_seed.enabled=false` | Yes | No | `TestBL387_ChildPRD_NoInheritance_WhenSeedDisabled` | Must not fire for disabled parent |
| `memoryScopeSeedFn` maxEntries capped at 50 | Yes | No | `TestBL387_ChildPRD_InheritanceCappedAt50` | Hard cap regardless of parent MaxPerScope |
| `SetMemoryVerifierFn` wires callback on Manager | Yes | No | Used in all Verifier tests above | Production wire-up in main.go pending Phase 2 integration |
| `SetMemoryScopeSeedFn` wires callback on Manager | Yes | No | Used in all ChildPRD tests above | Production wire-up in main.go pending Phase 2 integration |

## Capacity-aware admission for interactive sessions + verifier; session-delete memory strategy; capacity-card fixes (2026-09-29/30)

Operator-reported while diagnosing why PRD a2833a5e's verifier used a weak
model and why its capacity card showed an unrelated node: (1) a genuine data
race in daemon-restart boot-resume that could kill a live in-flight session;
(2) capacity ledger only ever listed nodes/pools an operator had explicitly
capped, and `/api/capacity` was never scoped to a specific PRD; (3)
interactive session starts and the verifier's own `/api/ask` call had zero
capacity interaction at all; (4) verifier backend/model always fell back to
a hardcoded `ollama` default, ignoring the PRD's own backend; (5) found and
fixed a real pre-existing data-loss bug in `PurgeScope`/`ArchiveScope` while
wiring session-delete's memory strategy (session-local purge/archive
discarded the session ID and operated on the whole project).
