| SEC-009: narrowed `federation-peer` default grant + new `/peers/self` | **Yes** | **Yes** | `TestFederationPeer_DefaultCaps`, `TestFedCap_PeerTokenAccepted_SEC009`, `TestFedCap_PeerToken_CustomGroup_SessionsList`; smoke §60 | Smoke §60 **skips** against the default (empty-admin-token) sandbox — with no admin token, `fedAuthMiddleware`'s empty-token early-return makes every caller admin-equivalent regardless of which Bearer token was presented, so peer-vs-admin has nothing to distinguish. **Manually validated against a real authenticated sandbox** (`server.token` set): create → `token_present:true`/no raw token; `GET /peers/self` as the peer → 200, own entry; `GET /api/sessions` with the same bare peer token → 403 (narrowed grant confirmed live, not just in a unit test) |
| SEC-006: `?token=` removed from REST/WS/MCP SSE; replaced by header, WS `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`, or a single-use nonce on the 3 browser-GET-only routes | **Yes** | **Yes** | `nonce_test.go` (5), `nonce_auth_test.go` (6), `ws_sec006_test.go` (3, incl. a real client-side RFC 6455 subprotocol-echo check via `gorilla/websocket`'s own `Dialer`), `TestMCPFedAuth_QueryParamToken_Rejected`; `app-nonce.test.js` (6, PWA-side); smoke §61 | Smoke §61's `?token=`-rejection and nonce-round-trip checks **skip** against the default empty-admin-token sandbox (same reason as S60 — nothing to reject when every caller already passes through). The no-auth nonce-mint check runs in both postures but expects a *different* code each way — 400 ("no caller token") under the empty-token bypass, 401 (rejected by `fedAuthMiddleware` before the handler runs at all) once a real token is set — caught via live testing after the smoke script initially assumed 400 in both cases. **Manually validated against a real authenticated sandbox**: no-auth nonce mint → 401 (not 400); `?token=<admin>` with no header → 401; minted nonce → `/api/files/download?nonce=...` authenticates (400 missing-path, not 401); same nonce reused → 401 (single-use confirmed live); a valid nonce on `/api/sessions` (not in the allow-list) → 401 |

## PWA WebSocket liveness watchdog (operator-reported 2026-10-06) — v8.61.2

Operator: "sent a command after being idle for a few minutes and had to exit the session and go back in for it to start moving again." Root cause: `ws.readyState` can stay `OPEN` after a NAT/proxy silently drops an idle TCP mapping — no `close`/`error` event ever fires (nothing on the wire tells the browser), so `scheduleReconnect()` — which only ran from those two event handlers — never triggered. The daemon's `MsgPing`→`pong` handler already existed (`internal/server/api.go`) but the PWA client never sent one.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `_wsIsStale(lastActivityAt, now)` — pure staleness decision (no I/O) | **Yes** | No | 4 tests in `internal/server/web/app-ws-watchdog.test.js`: fresh activity not stale, exactly-at-threshold not yet stale (boundary is strict `>`), just-over-threshold is stale, minutes-of-silence (the reported scenario) is stale | Extracted from the `setInterval` callback specifically so it's testable — the stub browser environment this test suite uses no-ops `setInterval` entirely |
| `_wsSendPing()` — sends `{"type":"ping"}` only when `readyState === OPEN` | **Yes** | No | 2 tests: sends when OPEN, does nothing (and doesn't throw) when CONNECTING or `state.ws` is `null` | — |
| Full round trip: client ping → server pong → `wsLastActivityAt` refreshed | No | **Yes** | Playwright against a real daemon: captured actual WS frames over a real 20s `WS_PING_INTERVAL_MS` cycle — confirmed exactly one `{"type":"ping"}` sent and one `{"type":"pong"}` received | — |
| Watchdog forces a reconnect when activity truly stops (simulating a dead-but-still-OPEN socket) | No | **Yes** | Playwright: froze `state.wsLastActivityAt` via a property getter/setter that swallows all writes (a naive one-time backdate isn't a valid simulation — the daemon's 5s periodic `stats` broadcast would overwrite it before the watchdog's next tick, which is in fact why the first version of this live test gave a false negative and had to be corrected to actually block every frame, not just pings, from refreshing the clock). Confirmed: the stale connection closed and a fresh one opened within one `WS_PING_INTERVAL_MS` tick. | Live test script not retained (ad hoc verification, deleted after use per the project's temp-file convention) — the pure-function unit tests above pin the same decision logic permanently |

## GH#179 — LLM registry `api_key_ref` read-path redaction — v8.63.1

A literal `api_key_ref` (as opposed to a `${secret:name}` reference) was
returned in clear text by `GET /api/llms`, `GET /api/llms/{name}`, and
the `llm_list`/`llm_get` MCP tools (both proxy to the same REST handler).
Fixed by mirroring the existing SEC-014 federation-peer redaction
pattern (`multiserver.Entry.Redacted()`/`RedactedList()`) one-for-one:
`inference.LLM.Redacted()`/`RedactedList()`. A changed response contract
(two new fields) per the Testing Tracker Rule.

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |

| `inference.LLM.Redacted()` — clears a literal `api_key_ref`, sets `api_key_ref_present`/`api_key_ref_prefix` | **Yes** | No | `TestLLM_Redacted_ClearsLiteralKey` in `internal/inference/llm_test.go`: literal key cleared, prefix is first 4 chars, original struct untouched (copy semantics) | — |
| `inference.LLM.Redacted()` — leaves a `${secret:name}` reference as-is | **Yes** | No | `TestLLM_Redacted_LeavesSecretRefAsIs`: a secret reference names a secret, it doesn't contain one, so it's safe to echo back (same reasoning as the existing `websearchAPIKeyRefs`/DNS-01 `dns01TokenSecretRef` convention) | — |
| `RedactedList()` | **Yes** | No | `TestRedactedList`: mixed literal + secret-ref entries, input slice not mutated | — |
| `GET /api/llms` / `GET /api/llms/{name}` never echo a literal key | **Yes** | No | `TestHandleLLMs_List_RedactsLiteralAPIKey`, `TestHandleLLMs_GetSingle_RedactsLiteralAPIKey` in `internal/server/gh179_llm_api_key_redaction_test.go`: response body byte-searched for the literal value, must be absent | `llm_list`/`llm_get` MCP tools proxy this same REST handler — fixed by the same change, not independently tested |
| `GET /api/llms` still shows a `${secret:name}` reference | **Yes** | No | `TestHandleLLMs_List_LeavesSecretRefVisible` | — |
| `PUT /api/llms/{name}` preserves a stored literal key when the client omits `api_key_ref` (the redacted-GET-echoed-back case) | **Yes** | **Yes** (a real regression this fix would otherwise have introduced) | `TestHandleLLMs_Put_PreservesLiteralKey_OnUnrelatedEdit`: reproduces the exact GET→edit-unrelated-field→PUT round trip the PWA and the `llm_add_model`/`llm_remove_model` MCP tools (`internal/mcp/inference.go`) both perform; PUT handler changed from a zero-valued decode to decode-onto-a-copy-of-the-existing-entry, matching the pre-existing `fedPeerUpdate` merge pattern | Without this companion fix, redacting the GET response would silently wipe every literal API key on the next unrelated edit |
| `PUT /api/llms/{name}` with an explicit `"api_key_ref": ""` still clears the key on purpose | **Yes** | No | `TestHandleLLMs_Put_ExplicitEmptyClearsKey` | Confirms the merge-onto-existing fix doesn't make the key impossible to intentionally clear |

No Playwright pass done for this specific field — follows the same node-test-only coverage pattern as the rest of this form |

| `RemoteDispatcher.SetStore(store)` + `effectiveServers()` — once wired, every dispatch method (`HasServers`, `refreshCache`, `ForwardCommand`, `ForwardHTTP`, `ListAllSessions`) reads the live `multiserver.Store` on every call instead of the frozen construction-time slice; falls back to the static snapshot when no store has been wired yet (startup window, and direct-construction unit tests) | **Yes** | No | `TestEffectiveServers_SetStoreSeesRuntimeAddedPeer`, `TestEffectiveServers_LiveUpdateOverridesStaleView`, `TestEffectiveServers_FallsBackToStaticSnapshotBeforeSetStore` (`internal/proxy/remote_test.go`); full existing suite (10 tests) still green; `-race -count=3` clean | `NewRemoteDispatcher` is now always constructed in `main.go` (previously gated on `len(cfg.Servers) > 0`, which meant a daemon with zero YAML-seeded servers but dynamically-added peers had no dispatcher at all) |
| CLI `--server <name>`: `daemonAPIURL`/`daemonHTTPClient` used to resolve the name by scanning this *separate CLI process's* own YAML-loaded `cfg.Servers` — same staleness gap, plus it needed to hold the remote's plaintext token in this short-lived process for no reason. Now always targets the *local* daemon and routes through its existing `/api/proxy/<name>/<path>` passthrough (already correct — merges YAML + live store, injects the remote's stored token server-side) | **Yes** | No | `TestDaemonAPIURL_ServerFlagRoutesThroughLocalProxy`, `TestDaemonAPIURL_NoServerFlagTargetsLocalCommand`, `TestDaemonAPIURL_ExplicitURLFlagWins`, `TestDaemonHTTPClient_ServerFlagUsesLocalToken` (`cmd/datawatch/daemon_api_url_test.go`) | Behavior change from before this fix: an unknown/disabled `--server` name used to silently fall back to `localhost` with a stderr warning (so a command could silently run on the *wrong* daemon without the operator noticing); now the local proxy returns an explicit 404 instead — a deliberate improvement, not an incidental side effect |
| Full live round trip: two real daemons, a peer added to one via `federation peer add` while both are already running, then a cross-host `send` or `datawatch session list --server <name>` from the CLI | No | No | — | Not live-verified in this pass — the unit tests above exercise the exact live-vs-frozen dispatch mechanism the live scenario depends on (`SetStore`/`effectiveServers`, and the proxy passthrough, which already had its own coverage) |

## Guardrail verdict decision log

Every guardrail verdict, judged or deterministic, is now recorded as a `guardrail_verdict`
Decision on the Automaton. A blocked Automaton also says why it is blocked. This is a
server-side change only; no client displays it yet.

Contract changes:

- `blocked_reason` (string, `omitempty`) on automaton objects (`PRD.BlockedReason`). It is set only
  while the automaton is blocked by a guardrail verdict. It is cleared when the automaton leaves a
  blocked status.
- `judge_session_id` (string, `omitempty`) on decision entries (`Decision`) and on guardrail verdicts
  (`GuardrailVerdict`). It names the session that ran the guardrail judge.
- `judge_output_path` (string, `omitempty`) on guardrail verdicts (`GuardrailVerdict`). It names the
  judge output file, which is kept until the verdict save succeeds.
- New decision kind `guardrail_verdict`, appended by `recordGuardrailVerdict` at the four guardrail
  sites: task-level, per-story, rules-review and ci-watch.

## Model/backend pairing — endpoint contract change

Changed endpoint contract. The PRD create, PRD LLM, story LLM, task LLM and
verification/guardrail set endpoints now return `400` with the mismatch text
when a model does not pair with its backend (a bare Claude alias on `pi` or
`pi-prompt`, or a provider-tagged model on `claude-code`). Before this change
they accepted the pair and the session later exited with no output. A PRD
Run also refuses a PRD whose unfinished tasks contain a mismatched pair, so
records written earlier are refused too. The `pi-prompt` backend prints
`DATAWATCH_PI_FAILED` instead of `DATAWATCH_COMPLETE` on a non-zero exit or an
empty run.

Two levels: the Go tests, and the **model/backend live check** row, which
needs a running daemon. Leave the live row at Validated=No until the next task
has run against a sandbox daemon.

| PRD create with a bare Claude alias on pi is refused; set PRD LLM, story LLM, task LLM and verification/guardrail setters refuse a mismatch and leave the record unchanged | **Yes** (`TestModelBackendRefusalCreatePRDClaudeAliasOnPi`, `TestModelBackendRefusalSetPRDLLMLeavesRecordUnchanged`, `TestModelBackendRefusalSetStoryLLMLeavesRecordUnchanged`, `TestModelBackendRefusalSetTaskLLMUsesEffectiveBackend`, `TestModelBackendRefusalVerificationSetterRefused`, `TestModelBackendRefusalAcceptsValidVerificationPair` in `internal/autonomous/model_backend_refusal_test.go`) | No | `go test` in `internal/autonomous`; in-process Manager | Decomposition model is not checked (`TestModelBackendRefusalDecompositionModelNotChecked`). |

## Inference-cap gap closure — per-LLM `plan_tier` caps, verify lease hand-off, decompose admission, await-external — unreleased

Changed behavior: each LLM entry gains an optional `plan_tier` (subscription tier) and its `llm:<name>` pool limit resolves `max_inflight` → tier table (`autonomous.plan_tier_max_inflight`) → kind default; a task in verify keeps the worker's lease (re-keyed to `verify:<task>`) instead of a second one; decompose takes a planner lease on the same pools (host excluded); a task parked on an external condition releases its lease (and the tree lock when fully pushed) and is re-admitted through the normal bounded wait.

## PWA terminal disposed-guard and quiet service-worker line — unreleased

## Reactive usage back-off — Phase 4 surfaces, admission gate and staleness guard — unreleased

A per-backend, in-memory flag (`internal/autonomous/backoff.go`) that holds autonomous dispatch to a rate-limited backend; set automatically on `StateRateLimited` and by operators, cleared at the parsed reset time or after `autonomous.backoff_max_wait_minutes`. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md`. Howto: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md` (`## Reactive usage backoff`). Unit/integration run 2026-10-22: `go test ./internal/autonomous/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/mcp/ ./internal/router/ ./cmd/datawatch/ ./internal/session/ -run 'UsageBackoff|Backoff|PatternsVersion|RateLimitPatterns|GlobalCooldown|Guard_|Fingerprint' -count=1` — 90 passed.
Unit/integration run 2026-10-22 (extended drift-guard smoke, `.datawatch/verify/smoke-extended-drift-guard.sh`): `go test ./internal/session/ ./internal/autonomous/ ./internal/server/ ./internal/mcp/ ./internal/router/ ./cmd/datawatch/ -run 'ClaudeCLI|PatternsVersion|PatternsStale|RateLimitPatterns|UsageBackoff|Backoff|Capacity' -count=1` — passed (6/6 package suites `ok`: session, autonomous, server, mcp, router, cmd/datawatch). ## BL428 Phase 5 — per-LLM dollar-window budget (ceiling, ledger, admission gate, surfaces, peer opt-in) — unreleased

An LLM entry gains an optional `budget` (a dollar ceiling over a rolling `hours` window or a weekly `weekday` + `time` + `zone` window). A persisted spend ledger (`<data_dir>/autonomous/budget-ledger.jsonl`) is fed by a usage-event hook in the session cost path; when the window is full, autonomous admission for that LLM waits with the reason `budget window full: …` and resumes by itself when the window rolls over. Interactive session starts are never gated. `allocation_pct` is an opt-in, always-estimated share-of-allocation figure and never blocks. Peer spend counts only for peers named in `peer_window` (off by default) and fails open. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md` (Phase 5). Howto: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md` (`## Per-LLM dollar budget`). Live rows stay No until a sandbox daemon run.

## BL431 Phase 5: Automation BudgetPolicy — unreleased

An Automation carries an optional `budget_policy` (dollar ceiling, window, pacing, on-breach rule, reset anchors, optional allocation estimate, optional opted-in peers), and a member may carry a narrower override plus an `estimated_cost_usd`. A pure evaluator (`AutomationBudget`, `internal/autonomous/automation_budget.go`) reads the shared cost rollup (`PRDCostUSD` / `AutomationSpendUSD`, built on the existing spend ledger — no second ledger). The coordinator checks it before it starts any member (advance, activation entry, fork) and the admit hook holds new member tasks at a dollar ceiling. On a breach the Automation pauses and resumes by itself at the window rollover only when the reset time is known, otherwise it goes to blocked and waits for the operator; an alert is raised either way. `allocation_pct` is an optional estimate and never gates. Another daemon's spend counts only for peers named in `peer_window`, without automatic confirmation. Surfaces: `POST /api/automations/{id}/set_budget`, MCP `automation_set_budget`, `datawatch automation set-budget`, comm `automation set-budget`; the computed `budget` view on `automation_get` / `automation_list` / `GET /api/automations/{id}` and on each `autonomous_status` Automation row; audit events `automation_set_budget`, `automation_budget_breach`, `automation_budget_resumed`. Design: `docs/plans/2026-10-14-automation-orchestration-design.md` (Phase 5). Howto: `docs/howto/automata-capacity.md` (`## Automation spending limit`). All time-dependent tests use an injected clock.

**Live validation status: no live daemon smoke has been run for this phase.** Every Validated cell below is No and stays No until a sandbox daemon run exercises each row (set a small ceiling on an Automation, run members, and watch the pause, the automatic resume and the block). The unit tests drive a real `Manager`, `Coordinator` and httptest server with fake clocks, but not a running daemon with real sessions and real spend.

## Visibility, audit and parity close-out — unreleased

Waiting tasks gain a machine-readable wait cause, a plain-language reason, an optional reset time and a holder; running tasks gain their holdings; `GET /api/capacity` gains a `tasks` object (`waiting`, `running`) and `reset_known` on each back-off entry; the session status `automaton` block gains `wait_cause`, `wait_resets_at`, `holds` and `holds_note`. The capacity gate writes audit events (admission wait and release, back-off set and clear, budget wait, resume and rollover) with an injectable clock for the tests. One audit query filter set (`actor`, `action` with a trailing-`*` prefix form, `subject`, `session_id`, `since`, `until`, `limit`) is shared by REST, MCP, the CLI and the comm channel. The PWA gets a capacity and budget card plus cause chips and a Holds line. The Unit column is Yes for every row; every Live row stays No until a sandbox daemon run of release-smoke section 77.

## BL568 — Resource fingerprint exchange between federated peers (BL428 §3c/§4e) — not released

Two daemons that both opt the other in (the per-peer `fingerprint_sync` flag
on both sides) periodically exchange **hashes** of their shared-resource
fingerprints — compute-node identity from the node itself (GPU UUID, or cloud
instance ID) and the LLM-entry label (`billing_group`) that bills against one
account across peers. A hit becomes a **pending match record**; only when the
operator confirms it do the two daemons treat the resource as one shared pool,
and a confirmed shared compute node means the peer's admitted hold counts
against local admission capacity (peer outage fails open, logs once per
episode). Rejecting keeps (or makes) the resources separate. Raw values
(names, addresses, the billing-group label, tokens) never leave the daemon;
peer-token holders without the `federation:fingerprint` capability (only in
the full-control set) cannot read the exchange endpoint at all. Design doc:
[2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md](plans/2026-10-14-concurrency-and-budget-design.md)
§"Resource fingerprint exchange (sections 3c and 4e) — shipped"; operator howto:
[federation-fingerprint.md](howto/federation-fingerprint.md).

| Interface / Endpoint | Tested | Validated | Test Conditions | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Node identity — stable per node across two addresses; different across two nodes; GPU UUID preferred with cloud instance ID fallback; a node with no source is skipped entirely; names and addresses are never inputs | **Yes** (`TestResolveSameNodeTwoAddresses`, `TestResolveDifferentNodesDiffer`, `TestResolvePrefersGPUUUID`, `TestResolveFallsBackToInstanceID`, `TestResolveNoSourceSkipped`, `TestResolveIgnoresNameAndAddress` in `internal/fingerprint/identity_test.go`) | **No** | Pure functions, faked hardware sources | The identity is the node's own value, never an operator-set name |
| Pair key + hashes — the key differs per peer credential; the hash is stable for the same input, different per peer pair (A↔B ≠ A↔C) and per kind (node vs billing group); bad input rejected | **Yes** (`TestPairKeyDiffersPerToken`, `TestHashStableForSameInput`, `TestHashDiffersPerPeerPair`, `TestHashDiffersPerKind`, `TestHashRejectsBadInput` in `internal/fingerprint/hash_test.go`) | **No** | Pure functions | Per-pair hashes are the only identities that leave the daemon — neither side can reverse one into the other's value |
| Node export — entry without identity skipped; `billing_group` hashed in place; no raw field ever in an export item | **Yes** (`TestExportSkipsNodesWithoutIdentity`, `TestExportBillingGroupHashed`, `TestExportItemsCarryNoRawValues` in `internal/fingerprint/export_test.go`) | **No** | Fixed node fixtures | The payload is hashes only |

## Readable holder names — capacity endpoint contract — unreleased

`GET /api/capacity` resolves raw holder ids into operator-readable names and adds them **beside** the unchanged raw id fields: `holder_names` on `node:` pools (parallel to the untouched `holders`/`holder`), `holder_name` on each lease and waiting entry, and `readable`/`short_id` beside `task_id` on `tasks.waiting`/`tasks.running` (`readable_reason` next to `reason` for waiting tasks that name holders). The name object carries `id`, `kind`, `task_title`, `prd_id`, `prd_title`, `short_id` and `readable`; the never-truncated long form `full` appears only with `?long=1`. A resolved holder without a title falls back to the raw id in the API and to the localized `(untitled <short id>)` label in the PWA. The session status `automaton` block gains `wait_reason_readable` beside `wait_reason`; the CLI/comm formatter prefers the readable line and falls back to the raw id for older bodies. The `capacity_name_untitled` and `capacity_name_prd` keys exist in all five locale bundles (`en.json`, `de.json`, `es.json`, `fr.json`, `ja.json`) with real translations. The Unit column is Yes for every row below; every Live row stays No until a sandbox daemon click-through of the capacity card.

## Session store and PRD store

One record per session (`sessions.d/`) and per PRD (`autonomous/prds/`), a coalescing background writer, an archive file and a per-field size cap. Operator guide: `docs/operations.md` (Session and PRD storage layout). Plan and numbers: `docs/plans/2026-10-23-session-store-write-amplification.md`.

Unit results, 2026-10-23: `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestStore' ./internal/session/` and `go test -race -count=1 -run 'TestPRDStore' ./internal/autonomous/` pass with no race reports. The full `go test -race ./internal/autonomous/` passes (27 s). The full `go test -race ./internal/session/` fails 11 tests (`TestOneShot*`, `TestRestart*`, `TestResumeMonitorsAdopts_*`) on data races between the screen-capture goroutine (`manager.go`) and test code reading the session pointer from `store.Get` without a lock; the same tests fail the same way on `main` (checked with `git archive main`), so they are not caused by the store change and are left for a separate fix.

Live validation, 2026-10-23: a daemon built from this branch ran with a throwaway data directory and config, port 18081, no TLS, `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR`, never the production daemon. The data directory started with an old `sessions.json` of four sessions (two finished 30 days ago, two recent). First start: `sessions.json.pre-records.bak` and `sessions.d/LAYOUT` appeared, `sessions.json` was removed, the two old finished sessions moved to `sessions-archive.jsonl`, `GET /api/sessions?view=summary` returned the two recent ones, `?history=1` returned all four, and `GET /api/sessions/<archived id>` returned the archived session. A new shell session created a third record within the flush interval. Creating a PRD with a 90 KB spec wrote `autonomous/prds/<id>.json` and one side file, and `GET` returned the PRD. SIGTERM stop and restart kept every record.

## PRD commit scope: staging bounded to declared write dirs

Changed behavior: a PRD task session's auto-commit stages only the files under the PRD's declared write dirs (the spawn request's write scope, forwarded into the session's `WriteScope`); a worktree-mode PRD's scope is its own worktree; and a direct-mode PRD with no declared write dirs gets no git activity at all (new `prdAutoCommits` gate in `internal/autonomous/executor.go`), so it does not auto-commit the whole project directory. Report: `docs/plans/2026-10-23-prd-commit-scope-verification.md`.

| `POST /api/plugins/{name}/widgets/token` (**behaviour change**: was `config:write`) | `plugin:write` | **Yes** (`TestPluginWidgetsFedCap`, same subtests — a plugin:read-only peer gets `403`) | No | Same setup | **Validated=No.** |
| `POST /api/plugins/{name}/widgets/{widget_id}` push | plugin push token (unchanged, not a federation cap) | **Yes** (existing `TestPluginWidgets_Push*` in `internal/server/plugin_widgets_test.go`, unchanged) | No | — | Unchanged by this release. |
| Plugin lifecycle routes (`GET /api/plugins/{name}` etc., `internal/server/plugins.go`) | `config:read` / `config:write` (unchanged) | **Yes** (`TestPluginLifecycleFedCapUnchanged` — config-only peer `200`, plugin-only peer `403`) | No | Same setup | Confirms the new caps did not leak onto lifecycle routes. |
| `plugin:read` / `plugin:write` absent from every built-in group except `full-control` | — | **Yes** (`TestPluginCaps_NotInDefaultPresets` in `internal/federation/capabilities_test.go`) | No | Iterates `ListBuiltinGroups()` and `Resolve()`s each | Least privilege: granted only via a custom group. |
| Gates for this release | — | — | — | `bash scripts/check-no-internal-refs.sh`; `node --check internal/server/web/app.js`; `make build`; `go test ./...`; `make lint` | See the v9.0.50 commit body for results. |

**Mobile parity:** N/A. No PWA change (`git diff main...HEAD -- internal/server/web` is empty). The `datawatch-app` mobile client authenticates with the operator bearer token (`server.token`, see `docs/api/mobile-surface.md`), not as a federation peer, so `fedCap` never restricts it and its widget reads behave exactly as before.

**Federation parity:** REST — yes (the three widget endpoints above). MCP / CLI / comm — none yet: no widget surface exists on those channels, so there is nothing to gate; the matching `mcp_tool_caps.go` entries arrive with the widget tools in the plan's later full-parity phase. PWA — uses the operator token, so it is not federation-gated. Per-session scoped credentials (`session-default`) never carried `config:*` and do not carry `plugin:*`, so sessions are unaffected.

## SSE stall detector scope (opencode family only)

Operator notes: `cmd/datawatch/sse_stall.go` (family gate, error-line matcher, fresh-text rule, shared end-reason helper) and `docs/llm-backends.md` (SSE stalls on local models). Both the verifier wait loop and the automata watchdog scan through the one shared entry point, and a match ends the session with the matched line, backend family and scan source recorded in the end reason. Validated stays **No**: a live opencode stall and a live Claude worker printing the phrase have not been observed against a running daemon.

## Worker idle nudge work-child guard and adopted sessions — unreleased

Operator notes: `cmd/datawatch/session_idle_probe.go` (work-child walk and own-server matching), `internal/autonomous/worker_nudge.go` and `worker_nudge_step.go` (the one nudge decision shared by the fresh and adopted waits), and `internal/autonomous/adopt_wait.go` (adopted-session wait). Changed behavior: only work children block an idle nudge (a process the claude-code runner started, such as a build or test run); the runner and the session's own MCP and channel servers do not. A worker adopted after a daemon restart is nudged, stalled and recorded on the same schedule as a fresh one, and a nudge seeded from a persisted event is never resent. Each `nudge_events` entry carries `session_id` and an outcome (`sent`, `answered` or `stalled`). Validated stays **No** until the live rows below run against a sandbox daemon.

## Post-turn nudge for idle claude-code workers — unreleased

Operator notes: `cmd/datawatch/post_turn_nudge.go` (the post-turn wait's nudge unit: the backend family is read on every tick until the session is visible; wait-start and family-resolved lines; the one-time window warning), `cmd/datawatch/worker_nudge_hooks.go` (the hooks shared by the fresh and adopted waits), `cmd/datawatch/end_attribution.go` (idle-detector end reason with the session's nudge history), `internal/autonomous/worker_nudge.go` (idle clock runs from the start of the idle run; the log-file age no longer shortens it), `internal/autonomous/worker_nudge_step.go` (answered and stall log lines, `NudgeStallError`, the stall retry reason) and `internal/session/completion_summary.go` (template placeholders are not completions). Changed behavior: the nudge applies to every claude-code worker in the post-turn wait whatever the task status shows, and a session that is not visible when the wait starts is nudged from its first visible tick. `GET /api/config` returns the effective nudge and stall windows as read-only keys. No REST, MCP, PWA or mobile surface changes beyond that read. Validated stays **No** until the live rows below run against a sandbox daemon; no live run was made for this section.

## Live held-task review — unreleased

Operator notes: `internal/autonomous/review_wake.go` (the per-Automaton wake channel and its pending flag), `internal/autonomous/api.go` (`ResolveTaskReview` signals a live executor instead of waiting for it, and the run goroutine takes a decision that arrived at exit), and `internal/autonomous/executor.go` (the re-scan in the one-task-at-a-time walk and in the concurrent coordinator). Contract change on REST `resolve_task_review`, MCP `autonomous_prd_resolve_task_review` and CLI `datawatch autonomous resolve-review`: the 400 "executor is still finishing; try again shortly" answer no longer occurs while the Automaton is running, and there is no five second wait. The comm channel command `autonomous review-task` posts to the same REST route and changes in the same way; it has no test of its own for this change. All Go tests below were run and pass. No live connection test was run, so every row stays Validated: No. Plan: `docs/plans/2026-10-25-live-held-task-review.md`.

## Session tags (own tags, inherited tags, tags route) — unreleased

Operator notes: `internal/session/tags.go` (own tags, inherited tags, delete-in-use count), `internal/server/session_tags.go` (`POST /api/sessions/tags`, the tag wiring, the `inherited_tags` read view), and the `tags` field on the start request. ## Tag browsing: shared tag registry, attention contract, settings and the tag PWA pieces (unreleased)

Operator notes: `internal/tagregistry` (the registry core: keeper and peer roles, sync, forwarded writes, per-field conflicts, stale copies, pending sync, merge and removed-on-keeper notes, cache, commit order), `internal/server/tag_registry.go` (the registry routes and the `registry` object), `internal/server/tag_settings.go` and `internal/config/tags_settings.go` (the six `autonomous.tags` keys), and `cmd/datawatch/tag_registry_wiring.go` (boot wiring and the sync loop). Changed contracts: `GET /api/autonomous/tags` gains the `registry` object; `GET /api/autonomous/tags/registry` and `POST /api/autonomous/tags/registry/write` are new keeper-to-peer routes; `POST /api/autonomous/tags/registry/notes/{id}/dismiss` is new; the `tag_update` frame gains the `registry_synced` kind; the default attention statuses now include `paused`; the `autonomous.tags` keys are new (six). Operator guides: `docs/howto/automata-tags.md`, `docs/howto/automata-tag-registry.md`, flow `docs/flow/tag-registry-sync-flow.md`.

Both validation levels are listed. Every Tested row below was run on 2026-10-26 with Go 1.27.2 (linux/amd64) and Node v24.15.0 (Linux x86_64), from the repository root, with `env -u TMUX -u TMUX_TMPDIR` in front of each command. The Go tests use fakes, `httptest` and temporary directories; no test starts a live daemon, a peer or a keeper. The PWA rows are Node tests of the functions in `internal/server/web/app.js` over the bundle source, not a browser session. **No row is Validated by a unit test.** The one live browser run of the registry, `TS-824`, ran on this branch and failed on the pending-sync badge; its row in the Automata tags section is the live record.

## Unauthenticated listener startup warning — warn, `server.acknowledge_unauthenticated`, health `listeners`, diagnose `listener_*` checks

At every start the daemon logs one warning line per listener that is enabled, not token-protected, and bound to a non-loopback address. Covered listeners and the token/secret that protects them: `rest` (server.token), `rest_tls` (server.ttls), `mcp_sse` (mcp.token, or server.token when mcp.token is empty), `proxy_sandbox` (server.token — same gate as `rest`; warned when it is enabled and the token is empty), `webhook` (webhook.token), `github_webhook` (github_webhook.secret); `twilio_webhook` has no built-in auth and is never warned. The logged line names the listener and its configured bind address — deliberately, so the operator sees which listener and what it listens on — and never a token or secret value. `server.acknowledge_unauthenticated` (bool, default `false`) silences that warning for those listeners and sets their `acknowledged` flag in the `/api/health` `listeners` array and the `listener_*` diagnose detail; it does not change the bind address, the token, or the warning condition itself. Every listener's auth state is computed on every request from the config the server already holds (`config.ListenerAuthStates`) so the answer is never stale. The `/api/health` `listeners` array is deliberately posture only: no bind address and no token/secret value, because `/api/health` is reachable without authentication. The pre-existing `auth_required`, `mcp_auth_required` and `mcp_sse` fields are unchanged and remain pinned by the pre-existing `/api/health` state tests.

## Untyped markup bodies and nosniff on API responses — unreleased

The gzip middleware in front of every `/api` route (`internal/server/api_gzip.go`) changed what a client receives in two cases. (1) A response with no `Content-Type` whose first bytes read as HTML, XML or SVG is sent as `text/plain; charset=utf-8`, its body is HTML-escaped (`<` `>` `&` `"` `'`), and the `Content-Length` the handler declared is dropped because the escaped body is longer. (2) Every response carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, set before the status line is written; a handler that set the header itself keeps its value. JSON, other typed bodies and anything with a `Content-Encoding` are not altered, and a `Write` still reports the caller's byte count when the body was escaped. The MCP debug transport (`internal/mcp/transport_debug.go`) pins the same header and escapes a stream whose type is missing or HTML; a `text/event-stream` keeps its JSON meaning: only `<` and `>` change, to the JSON escapes `\u003c` and `\u003e` (see the section "MCP debug transport: nosniff header and JSON-escaped event streams"). The commit-message and tag-message write path moved from `-m <text>` and a temporary file to git's standard input (`git commit -F -`, `git tag -a -F -`).

## MCP debug transport: nosniff header and JSON-escaped event streams — unreleased

The MCP SSE listener (`mcp.sse_port`) is wrapped by `ObserveSSEHandler` (`internal/mcp/transport_debug.go`). Its wire contract changed in three ways. (1) Every response from that listener carries `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`: a stream request (`GET` with `Accept: text/event-stream`) gets it from the observer before the first byte, and any other request (a `POST /message`, a `GET` with no such `Accept`) gets it before the handler runs. (2) A stream whose handler declared `text/event-stream` (what mcp-go does) is no longer passed through byte for byte: `<` and `>` are written as the JSON escapes `\u003c` and `\u003e`, which decode to the same string, and every other byte (including `&`, quotes and a literal `&lt;`) is unchanged. mcp-go already writes `<` and `>` that way inside its own JSON, so a JSON-RPC reply is identical on the wire; the change shows only for bytes mcp-go does not JSON-encode. (3) A stream whose handler set no type or an HTML type is re-typed `text/event-stream` and its payload is HTML-escaped. The REST side of the same change is in the section above.

The wire body has no `<` or `>`; the JSON value decodes to the original; `&`, quotes, an `event:` line and a literal `&lt;` arrive unchanged. | Unit (real server) | **Yes** | Pass | **No** | Read through a real `net/http` connection, not a recorder. |

*Monitoring and observability: why there is no stats field yet (B7).*

What the question store exposes today, and what an operator can read from it without any new field:

- **Audit trail**: every state change appends exactly one audit entry under its own action (`question_raised`, `question_answered`, `answer_superseded`, `question_withdrawn`, `question_expired` and `question_answer_refused`; six in all), each with a stable CEF name and severity. The raise, answer, supersede and withdraw counts over any window come from `GET /api/audit?action=<action>`; a secret-refused answer is audited without the answer text.
- **Queue depth and age**: `GET /api/questions?state=open` returns `count` and each question's `created_at`, so open-queue depth, the oldest open question, and the answered or withdrawn totals are all one filtered read (`state`, `context`, `asker`, `text` and `limit` filters). The daemon reads the append-only `questions.jsonl` in its data directory, so these numbers survive a restart.
- **Switch state**: `GET /api/config` reports `autonomous.questions.enabled`, and every endpoint answers 503 naming the switch while it is off.

Why no `SystemStats` field, `GET /api/questions/stats` endpoint, stats MCP tool, Monitor card or Prometheus counter is added in this step: step 1 is the record-keeping layer only (config + REST parity), questions have no deadline and nothing acts on them yet, so there is no rate, latency, error or saturation signal to chart. Every number a stats field would hold (counts by state, queue depth, oldest open age) is already derivable from the two reads above. A duplicate counter would add a second source of truth to keep in step with the store file. The store is a single append-only file with no goroutine, pool or retry loop, so there is no background work to monitor. The Monitor card, the stats MCP tool and the comm stats verb arrive with plan steps 2-3, when the queue view and the surface verbs make an open-question count something an operator watches; at that point the stats read the same store and are added with their tests. Until then the release smoke (section 83) and TS-827 exercise the surface end to end on a sandbox daemon.

## Node placement on the production entry shape — candidates, ledger spread, adoption — unreleased

The entry shape the rows protect is the one the running daemon actually carries: three single-node ollama LLM entries (one node each, one node shared by two entries), a pi-prompt entry whose own `compute_nodes` lists two of those nodes, and pi and opencode entries that claim no node. The previous unit fixtures were cleaner than production — fewer single-node entries of the same kind — and the tests that passed on them did not catch the placement stall. The post-deploy gate for the same shape is `scripts/check-waiter-nodes.sh` (daemon address and token via `DATAWATCH_URL` and `DATAWATCH_TOKEN`): it reports the node each waiter is bound to, prints an `OVERLIMIT` line with the lease holders for any node holding more engines than its limit, and exits 2 on either finding.

## Stuck-running watchdog and `autonomous.stuck_running_seconds` — v9.29.2

An Automaton that stays `running` with every task terminal, no live session and no executor is re-checked once after `autonomous.stuck_running_seconds` (default 900) and blocked after a second full bound. `GET /api/config` and `GET /api/autonomous/config` gain the `stuck_running_seconds` field and `PUT /api/config` accepts `autonomous.stuck_running_seconds` (whole seconds; zero stores zero and the default applies at read time; a negative value is ignored). The new audit action `autonomous_stuck_running_blocked` is emitted as JSON lines and CEF.
